book.book01.title: 1,000 Places to See Before You Die
book.book01.author: Patricia Schultz
book.book01.description: Nearly a thousand pages of markets, reefs, hill towns and hotel terraces worth crossing a continent for, each with the practical details attached. Dangerous to leave open near a bank account.
book.book02.author: Stephen King
book.book02.description: Behind a diner's pantry lies a door into the past, and the schoolteacher who steps through means to stop an assassination. Long, tender, and shrewd about how hard history shoves back when you shove it.
book.book03.title: 1st to Die
book.book03.author: James Patterson
book.book03.description: Newlyweds are being murdered in San Francisco, and the homicide inspector on the case builds her own off-books team of four women to crack it. Short chapters, fast pulse, first of a very long series.
book.book04.title: The 7 Stages of Grieving
book.book04.author: Wesley Enoch & Deborah Mailman
book.book04.description: One performer, seven movements, and a grief that belongs to a whole people rather than to one funeral. Australian Indigenous theatre mixing poetry, history and plain fury, all inside eighty pages.
book.book05.title: 84, Charing Cross Road
book.book05.author: Helene Hanff
book.book05.description: Twenty years of letters between a broke New York writer and a very correct London bookshop, mostly about secondhand editions and eventually about everything else. Short, wry, and it will get you.
book.book06.title: A Dance With Dragons
book.book06.author: George R. R. Martin
book.book06.description: Thousands of pages of armies crawling toward each other across two continents, with magic waking in the cold places and nobody safe from one chapter to the next. Epic in the exhausting, blood-soaked sense.
book.book07.title: A Deepness in the Sky
book.book07.author: Vernor Vinge
book.book07.description: Two human fleets circle a world of spider-like people racing through their own industrial revolution, and only one fleet means them well. Vast, patient, and full of genuinely strange wonder.
book.book08.title: Design Patterns; Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
book.book08.author: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson, J. Vlissides
book.book08.description: Twenty-three recurring solutions to problems every programmer meets twice, named and catalogued so a team can argue in shorthand. Dry as chalk, and still on the desk of everyone who builds software.
book.book09.title: A Dictionary of the English Language
book.book09.author: Samuel Johnson
book.book09.description: Every definition comes with a quotation to prove it, and the compiler's own opinions slip in more than once. A monument of a reference work, magnificently dry, and long since overtaken by the lexicographers who followed.
book.book10.title: A Fire Upon the Deep
book.book10.author: Vernor Vinge
book.book10.description: An old evil wakes in the high reaches of the galaxy, while two marooned children fall in among sword-carrying pack creatures on a medieval world. Enormous, strange, and worth every page.
book.book11.title: A Fire Upon the Deep
book.book11.author: James Lovegrove & Nancy Holder
book.book11.description: Wrongdoing, wisecracks and a caper unfolding a long way from any police station. Light company for one evening, one entry in a longer run, and generous enough to send you off grinning rather than grim.
book.book12.title: A Game of Thrones
book.book12.author: George R. R. Martin
book.book12.description: Seven kingdoms, one throne, and a dozen families willing to spend their children on it. Eight hundred pages of cold politics with dragons at the edges, and nobody is safe for being likeable.
book.book13.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
book.book13.author: Holly Jackson
book.book13.description: Pip picks a five-year-old murder case for her school project, mostly because she refuses to believe the boy everyone blames did it. Interview logs, teenage nerve, and a floor that keeps dropping.
book.book14.title: A Room of One's Own
book.book14.author: Virginia Woolf
book.book14.description: Money and a door that locks: the two things Woolf says a woman needs before she can write, argued in lectures that wander, joke, then land like a verdict. Slim, and still waiting for a decent answer.
book.book15.title: Rosalind Franklin; The Dark Lady of DNA
book.book15.author: Brenda Maddox
book.book15.description: The crystallographer whose images made the double helix possible, and whose credit went elsewhere, gets a careful full-length life here. Science, snobbery and X-ray film, with no rush to sainthood.
book.book16.title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
book.book16.author: Bill Bryson
book.book16.description: How big is the universe, how old are the rocks, and which lunatics worked it out? Six hundred pages of cheerful science writing that makes geology sound like very good village gossip.
book.book17.title: A Storm of Swords
book.book17.author: George R. R. Martin
book.book17.description: War splits into a dozen smaller wars, crowns change hands faster than anyone can swear loyalty, and magic keeps creeping in at the edges. Bleak, enormous, and the volume that teaches you not to get attached.
book.book18.title: A Study in Scarlet
book.book18.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
book.book18.description: Two men share rooms on Baker Street, and one of them can read a stranger's whole history off his boots. The case that starts the most famous partnership in crime, with a corpse and no wound.
book.book19.title: A Time to Kill
book.book19.author: John Grisham
book.book19.description: In a Mississippi town a father answers an unspeakable crime himself, and the lawyer defending him must sell that to a jury while the streets outside pick sides. Ugly, angry, impossible to read neutrally.
book.book20.title: A Wrinkle in Time
book.book20.author: Madeleine L'Engle
book.book20.description: Meg is bad at school, furious, and the only one who can fetch her father back from a planet where every house is identical. Three peculiar old women, a fold in space, and love as the last weapon.
book.book21.title: ABCC; A Bookstonbury Crochet Collection
book.book21.author: Various Authors
book.book21.description: Crochet your favourite Bookstonian icons and create your own pocket-sized version of our beautiful town! 120 easy-to-follow and cosy patterns, such as: St Bookston, Raw Fish, Seagull, Mobile Bookshop, Dog, Plants, and many more!
book.book22.title: Abridgment of Murray's English Grammar
book.book22.author: Lindley Murray
book.book22.description: Parsing, punctuation and the parts of speech, laid out for schoolrooms two centuries ago in the flattest voice imaginable. Arid, gloriously obsolete, and a treat if you collect such things.
book.book23.title: Ace; What Asexuality Reveals About Desire, Society and the Meaning of Sex
book.book23.author: Angela Chen
book.book23.description: Interviews and reporting on what asexuality actually is, and what a culture assuming everyone wants sex gets wrong about consent, romance and loneliness. Clear, generous and quietly radical.
book.book24.title: The Acts of King Arthur and His Noble Knights
book.book24.author: John Steinbeck
book.book24.description: Malory's knights are turned back into men who sweat, doubt and argue, in a retelling its author never lived to finish. Scholarly, affectionate, and strange in the best way for lovers of the old Arthur.
book.book25.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn; Adventures of Tom and Huck #2
book.book25.author: Mark Twain
book.book25.description: Down the Mississippi on a raft go a runaway boy and a runaway man, dodging frauds, feuds and the boy's own conscience. Funny, uncomfortable, and argued over in classrooms ever since.
book.book26.title: After the Funeral
book.book26.author: Agatha Christie
book.book26.description: The relatives gather for the will, someone says the old man was murdered, and within a day she is dead too. Poirot sorts the family's polite lies into order, and the answer will annoy you beautifully.
book.book27.title: Alanna; The First Adventure (The Song of the Lioness #1)
book.book27.author: Tamora Pierce
book.book27.description: Swapping places with her twin, a girl cuts her hair, calls herself Alan and starts the brutal business of page training, unwanted magic gift and all. Brisk, stubborn, and the opening of a knighthood.
book.book28.title: Alias Grace
book.book28.author: Margaret Atwood
book.book28.description: Convicted of murder as a servant girl, Grace Marks tells her story to a doctor who wants her mind mapped, and every telling shifts a little. Slippery, patient historical crime that never lets you settle.
book.book29.title: Alvar Aalto
book.book29.author: Alvar Aalto
book.book29.description: Slim, specialist and unapologetic about it: a mid-century account of one architect's work and the working life behind it. If modern buildings are your thing, here is a quiet afternoon well spent.
book.book30.title: Amadeus
book.book30.author: Peter Shaffer
book.book30.description: Onstage, an aging court composer confesses a lifetime of envy: he alone recognised the giggling, vulgar young genius, and he hated God for the choice. Wickedly funny about being merely competent.
book.book31.title: American Psycho
book.book31.author: Bret Easton Ellis
book.book31.description: A Wall Street banker itemises his suits, his business cards and his murders in the same flat voice. Genuinely sickening satire, not for the squeamish, and hard to shake once it is finished.
book.book32.title: Among the Hidden; (The Shadow Children #1)
book.book32.author: Margaret Peterson Haddix
book.book32.description: Third children are illegal, so Luke lives in an attic and watches the world through a vent, until a face in a neighbour's window changes what hiding costs. Short, tense, best not read before bed.
book.book33.title: Anathem
book.book33.author: Neal Stephenson
book.book33.description: Monks of mathematics live behind walls and keep time with clockwork rites, until something appears in the sky and they are sent out. Dense, invented vocabulary, and a puzzle that widens into worlds.
book.book34.title: Ancillary Justice; Imperial Radch #1
book.book34.author: Ann Leckie
book.book34.description: What is left of a warship's mind walks around in a single borrowed body, carrying a grudge against an empire that thinks in centuries. Cold, strange, and quietly furious about who counts as a person.
book.book35.title: And The World Spins Anyway
book.book35.author: Georgie Jones
book.book35.description: Barely more than a hundred pages of poems and quiet reflection, fond of weather and open ground, content to sit with a question rather than settle it. Gentle reading for an evening with nowhere to be.
book.book36.title: Angels & Demons
book.book36.author: Dan Brown
book.book36.description: Vatican City has hours to live, a stolen canister ticking somewhere beneath it, and a symbologist chasing an old brotherhood's markers across Rome at a dead sprint. Daft, propulsive, paced like a chase.
book.book37.title: Angels in America; A Gay Fantasia on National Themes
book.book37.author: Tony Kushner
book.book37.description: New York, the mid-1980s: a man with AIDS is left by his lover, a Mormon lawyer cannot stay closeted, and an angel comes through the ceiling. A two-part play that argues with God and with America at the same time.
book.book38.title: Animal Farm
book.book38.author: George Orwell
book.book38.description: The livestock throw out the farmer and write their own commandments, then watch the pigs quietly edit them. Short, cold and merciless about how a revolution eats itself. Nobody gets a happy field.
book.book39.title: The Animals of Farthing Wood
book.book39.author: Colin Dann
book.book39.description: Bulldozers take the wood, so badger, fox and a mob of frightened neighbours swear an oath and set out for a park they have only heard of. Plenty of them do not arrive. First leg of a long trek of sequels.
book.book40.title: Annabel Lee
book.book40.author: Edgar Allen Poe
book.book40.description: One short ballad, read aloud in minutes, where a grieving voice insists that the sea and the angels conspired to take his bride. Hypnotic rhyme, refrains that circle back, and a tomb by the shore at the end.
book.book41.title: Architecture in Britain; 1530-1830
book.book41.author: John N. Summerson
book.book41.description: Tudor great houses to Georgian terraces, sorted by patron, builder and style, with the plans to back it up. A scholarly survey for anyone who reads buildings the way others read novels, and a fine companion on a British tour.
book.book42.title: Ariel
book.book42.author: Sylvia Plath
book.book42.description: Late poems written at four in the morning, brilliant and furious and entirely unwilling to be comforted. Slim, difficult, and the collection that changed what a poem was allowed to sound like.
book.book43.title: Arnheim's Principles of Athletic Training; A Competency-Based Approach
book.book43.author: William E. Prentice
book.book43.description: A thousand pages of taping, prevention, rehab protocols and exam-ready competencies for the athletic trainer. Thorough, dry as chalk, and several editions behind current practice, though the anatomy has not moved.
book.book44.title: Around the World in Eighty Days
book.book44.author: Jules Verne
book.book44.description: An English gentleman bets his fortune that trains and steamers can carry him round the globe on schedule, then sets off with a bewildered French valet. Brisk, funny, and charmingly dated about the world.
book.book45.title: Art of the Modern Movie Poster; International Postwar Style and Design
book.book45.author: Various Authors
book.book45.description: Postwar cinema sold itself in ink: bold type, flat colour, faces cropped to a single stare. A big, generously plated survey of poster design country by country, for designers, film buffs and lovers of a specialist shelf.
book.book46.title: Artemis Fowl
book.book46.author: Eoin Colfer
book.book46.description: A twelve-year-old criminal mastermind kidnaps a fairy for ransom and learns that the fairies have better weapons than he does. Fast, cheeky, and the opening round of a very long feud.
book.book47.title: As Good As Dead
book.book47.author: Holly Jackson
book.book47.description: Pip has closed cases before, and now somebody is posting her taunts that quote one of them. The third turn of a small-town series where the sleuth is the one coming apart, and the bill for asking questions finally arrives.
book.book48.title: Ashfall Legacy; Ashfall #1
book.book48.author: Pittacus Lore
book.book48.description: Syd has spent his life hiding what his missing father was. When the truth finally arrives it comes with a starship, a treaty and a court of aliens who have plans for him. Fast science fiction adventure, and only the first book.
book.book49.title: Assassin's Apprentice; The Farseer Trilogy Book One
book.book49.author: Robin Hobb
book.book49.description: Taken in as the king's unacknowledged grandson, a boy is schooled in poisons, politics and a bond with animals nobody at court will admit exists. First of a long apprenticeship in growing up hard.
book.book50.title: Asterios Polyp
book.book50.author: David Mazzucchelli
book.book50.description: Lightning burns down the flat of a celebrated architect who never built anything, so he takes a bus to nowhere and learns to fix cars. A graphic novel where line, colour and lettering do the arguing.
book.book51.title: At the Earth's Core
book.book51.author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
book.book51.description: Drill straight down far enough and you break into a sunlit world beneath the crust, where men are cattle and telepathic reptiles hold the whip. Pulp adventure from the genre's early days, over in an afternoon.
book.book52.title: Atmosphere
book.book52.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
book.book52.description: Houston, the 1980s: an astronomer joins NASA's shuttle program and learns that the hard part of going to space is deciding who she can leave on the ground. A love story wired into a mission.
book.book53.title: Attack On Titan; Volume 1
book.book53.author: Hajime Isayama
book.book53.description: Humanity has spent a century behind three rings of wall, safe from giants that eat people for no reason anyone can name. This opening volume gets the outermost wall breached. Brutal, fast, and the start of something very long.
book.book54.title: Babel; or the Necessity of Violence
book.book54.author: R. F. Kuang
book.book54.description: Silver bars hold the meaning lost between two languages, and Oxford runs an empire on that power. Robin Swift, brought from Canton to translate, learns what the trade costs. Dense, angry historical fantasy about complicity.
book.book55.title: Beloved
book.book55.author: Toni Morrison
book.book55.description: A house outside Cincinnati is haunted by what slavery did, and by a young woman who turns up at the gate with no past. Ferocious, grief-soaked and not remotely comfortable. Read it slowly.
book.book56.title: Better Than the Movies
book.book56.author: Lynn Painter
book.book56.description: Liz will put up with the neighbour she cannot stand if it gets her a date with her childhood crush. Romantic comedy logic, a soundtrack running in the margins, and a heart that sneaks up on her.
book.book57.title: Call Me by Your Name
book.book57.author: André Aciman
book.book57.description: One Italian summer, a visiting scholar in the spare room, and a seventeen-year-old who notices everything and says nothing. Sun-drunk, aching prose about a season that does not come back.
book.book58.title: Camp Damascus
book.book58.author: Chuck Tingle
book.book58.description: America's most effective conversion camp boasts a spotless success rate, and Rose is beginning to see what it actually costs. Queer horror with teeth, furious at the institution, and still willing to grant its heroine daylight.
book.book59.title: Can't Spell Treason Without Tea; Tomes and Tea #1
book.book59.author: Rebecca Thorne
book.book59.description: A queen's guard and the most powerful mage in the realm quit their posts to open a bookshop that serves tea. Cozy fantasy with a dragon at the window, a town worth defending, and two women who would rather brew than fight.
book.book60.title: Cat's Eye
book.book60.author: Margaret Atwood
book.book60.description: A painter comes back to Toronto for a retrospective and finds the city crowded with the girls who tormented her at nine. A novel about how cruelty between small friends never quite finishes with you.
book.book61.title: Catcher in the Rye, The
book.book61.author: JD Salinger
book.book61.description: Kicked out of school again, a sixteen-year-old wanders New York for three days telling you exactly who is a phony and nothing at all about himself. Funny, exhausting, and sadder than it admits.
book.book62.title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
book.book62.author: Roald Dahl
book.book62.description: Five golden tickets, one sweet factory nobody has entered in years, and four children who richly deserve what happens to them. Charlie deserves better, and gets it. Delicious and slightly cruel.
book.book63.title: Charlotte's Web
book.book63.author: E. B. White
book.book63.description: Wilbur the pig has one winter to live, until the spider over his doorway starts writing advertisements for him in her web. Warm, funny barnyard company, and honest about goodbyes.
book.book64.title: Chemical Chaos; Horrible Science
book.book64.author: Nick Arnold & Tony De Saulles
book.book64.description: Acids, explosions and the genuinely disgusting history of chemistry, delivered with cartoons and no dignity whatsoever. Science smuggled in past the gag reflex, and children swallow it whole.
book.book65.title: Charmed Life; (Chrestomanci, Book 1)
book.book65.author: Diana Wynne Jones
book.book65.description: Cat Chant lets his sister handle the witchcraft, until both are taken in by an enchanter with nine lives and considerable style. Wry English magic where the quiet child turns out to matter most. First of the Chrestomanci books.
book.book66.title: Chemistry; The Central Science
book.book66.author: Theodore L. Brown
book.book66.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, thermodynamics and problem sets by the hundred, in the introductory textbook that raised a good many chemists. An early edition, so its data and diagrams belong to their moment rather than yours.
book.book67.title: The Chicago Manual of Style (CMOS)
book.book67.author: University of Chicago Press
book.book67.description: Hyphens, capitals, citations, proofreading marks: the house rulebook editors reach for mid-argument. This is an early edition of a reference revised many times since, so treat its verdicts as history rather than law.
book.book68.title: A Child's Garden of Verses
book.book68.author: Robert Louis Stevenson & Tasha Tudor
book.book68.description: Short rhymes about a swing, a shadow that will not keep step, and being sent to bed while it is still light outside. Nursery Victoriana, quaint in places, and lovely read aloud at any age.
book.book69.title: Children of Time; (Book 1)
book.book69.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
book.book69.description: A terraformed world was meant for monkeys. The uplift virus found spiders instead, and they have had millennia to build, while the last humans arrive in a dying ark. Patient, enormous science fiction about minds nothing like a human one.
book.book70.title: Chocolat; Book 1
book.book70.author: Joanne Harris
book.book70.description: Vianne Rocher opens a chocolate shop in a small French village on the first day of Lent, and the priest takes it personally. Warm, faintly witchy, and the first of a series worth staying in.
book.book71.title: Circe
book.book71.author: Madeline Miller
book.book71.description: Born to the sun god and useful to nobody, Circe learns what herbs and sheer will can do, and is exiled to an island for it. Greek myth told from the witch's side, with centuries of solitude and the mortals who wash ashore.
book.book72.title: Clap When You Land
book.book72.author: Elizabeth Acevedo
book.book72.description: A plane goes down between New York and the Dominican Republic, and two teenage girls learn they shared a father, and each other. A novel in verse, in two voices that circle grief until they can meet.
book.book73.title: Cleopatra and Frankenstein
book.book73.author: Coco Mellors
book.book73.description: Six months after meeting at a party, a broke British art student marries a rich New York ad man twice her age. What follows tracks that marriage, and the friends around it, through drink and depression.
book.book74.title: Collected Poems; 1934-1952
book.book74.author: Dylan Thomas
book.book74.description: Welsh hillsides, seaside dark, and a son telling his father not to go gentle: the poems Dylan Thomas chose to keep, gathered by his own hand. Sound first, sense second, and best read aloud.
book.book75.title: Confess
book.book75.author: Colleen Hoover
book.book75.description: Strangers post their confessions through an artist's door and he paints them. The woman who takes a job at his studio has secrets of her own, and a past she cannot afford to open. Romance with a sting.
book.book76.title: Conversations with Friends
book.book76.author: Sally Rooney
book.book76.description: Two student poets, a married couple who collect them, and email threads sharper than anything anyone says aloud. Cool, precise and quietly devastating about wanting to be chosen.
book.book77.title: Dark Age; (Red Rising #5)
book.book77.author: Pierce Brown
book.book77.description: Fifth in the Red Rising sequence, and the war has stopped looking winnable. Many voices, sieges that cost everything, and no guarantee your favourites survive. Eight hundred pages of bleak, bloody, propulsive space opera.
book.book78.title: The Dark is Rising
book.book78.author: Susan Cooper
book.book78.description: Will wakes on his eleventh birthday able to hear things nobody else can, and midwinter closes over the village in snow that is not weather. Six signs to find, and something very old hunting him for them.
book.book79.title: Dark Matter
book.book79.author: Blake Crouch
book.book79.description: Kidnapped by a masked man who knows far too much about his life, a physics professor wakes into a version of it he never lived. A thriller built on the roads not taken, and on what a man will do to get his own back.
book.book80.title: Dark Places
book.book80.author: Gillian Flynn
book.book80.description: Libby Day survived the night her family was slaughtered and testified against her own brother. Broke and out of sympathy years later, she takes money from murder hobbyists to go back and check. Mean, bleak, unputdownable.
book.book81.title: The Dark Portal; Book One of The Deptford Mice
book.book81.author: Robin Jarvis
book.book81.description: Beneath the streets of Deptford, mice keep to the daylight, because the sewers belong to rats who worship a cat as a god. Genuinely frightening for a children's book, and the opening of a grim animal trilogy.
book.book82.title: Death in Yellowstone; Accidents and Foolhardiness in the First National Park
book.book82.author: Lee H. Whittlesey
book.book82.description: Bears, bison, cliffs and above all the scalding springs: a park historian catalogues every way Yellowstone has killed a visitor, most of them avoidable. Grisly, meticulous, and the best argument ever made for staying on the boardwalk.
book.book83.title: Death Note; Volume 1
book.book83.author: Tsugumi Ohba
book.book83.description: Bored and brilliant, a top student finds a notebook that kills anyone whose name he writes in it, and decides the world needs pruning. First volume of a manga duel between a boy with a god complex and the detective reading his moves.
book.book84.title: Death of a Salesman; Certain Private Conversations in Two Acts and a Requiem
book.book84.author: Arthur Miller
book.book84.description: Willy Loman comes home with the car and his sample cases and cannot stop talking to people who are not in the room. Staged inside one exhausted head, memory cutting into kitchen argument, ending at a graveside.
book.book85.title: Death on the Nile
book.book85.author: Agatha Christie
book.book85.description: Heat, a pleasure steamer full of grudges, and a honeymoon that ends with a shot in the night. Poirot works through the passenger list while Egypt slides past the windows. Clever, and rather sad.
book.book86.title: Divergent
book.book86.author: Veronica Roth
book.book86.description: Chicago has sorted itself into five factions, and at sixteen you pick one for life. Beatrice's aptitude test refuses to sort her at all. Dystopian YA that moves fast, hits hard, and does not leave everyone standing.
book.book87.title: Down Under
book.book87.author: Bill Bryson
book.book87.description: Australia by train, beer and rented car: a country with a lovely temperament and more creatures that can kill you than anywhere else. Affectionate, funny, and stuffed with alarming history.
book.book88.title: Dracula
book.book88.author: Bram Stoker
book.book88.description: Letters, diaries and a ship's log assemble the case against a Transylvanian count who has quietly bought property in London. Victorian horror built as evidence rather than narration, and wonderfully patient about its dread.
book.book89.title: Dragonsong
book.book89.author: Anne McCaffrey
book.book89.description: Menolly's hold has no use for a girl who makes songs, so she runs, and ends up mothering nine newly hatched fire lizards. Warm, quick Pern story about a talent that will not be argued out of someone.
book.book90.title: Dreamer's Pool; Blackthorn & Grim #1
book.book90.author: Juliet Marillier
book.book90.description: Sprung from a filthy cell on the condition that she help anyone who asks, a bitter healer and her silent giant of a companion reach a woodland where a prince's bride is not quite who she was. Old Ireland, quiet magic, book one.
book.book91.title: The Dry; (Aaron Falk #1)
book.book91.author: Jane Harper
book.book91.description: Two years without rain, and a farming town buries a family it half believes shot itself. The federal investigator who comes home for the funeral left under a cloud of his own. Dust, grudges, and a whodunnit that keeps its cards.
book.book92.title: Emma
book.book92.author: Jane Austen
book.book92.description: Emma Woodhouse arranges everyone else's marriages with perfect confidence and no self-knowledge whatsoever. Wickedly funny about a comfortable village, and it ends as warmly as you hope.
book.book93.title: Empire of the Vampire
book.book93.author: Jay Kristoff
book.book93.description: Twenty-seven years without a sunrise, and the last of the silversaints tells his story from a cell to the vampire sent to write it down. Seven hundred pages of blood, black humour and holy war. Book one of a series.
book.book94.title: Fantastic Mr Fox
book.book94.author: Roald Dahl
book.book94.description: Three horrible farmers dig up a whole hillside to get at one fox, who simply digs better. Ninety-six pages of thieving, feasting and nerve, with the animals walking off with dinner.
book.book95.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
book.book95.author: Thomas Hardy
book.book95.description: Bathsheba inherits a farm and three men who want her: a shepherd who waits, a landowner who unravels, a soldier who charms. Sheep, harvest and weather get as many pages as the courtship, and not everyone survives.
book.book96.title: Feminist, Queer, Crip
book.book96.author: Alison Kafer
book.book96.description: What if a future without disability is not progress but erasure? A dense academic argument that crip politics and queer politics belong together, built for seminar readers rather than casual browsers.
book.book97.title: Femme in Public
book.book97.author: Alok V Menom
book.book97.description: Forty-six pages of poems about what it costs to walk down a street visibly femme, by a gender-nonconforming artist who does it daily. Short, furious, tender, and asking nobody for permission.
book.book98.title: Ficciones
book.book98.author: J. L. Borges, A. Bonner & A. Kerrigan
book.book98.description: Stories dressed as book reviews and encyclopedia entries: a library holding every possible book, a man who forgets nothing, an invented country that leaks into this one. Short, dry, and built to be reread.
book.book99.title: The Field Guide; The Spiderwick Chronicles #1
book.book99.author: Holly Black & Tony DiTerlizzi
book.book99.description: Three children, one crumbling family estate, and a hidden field guide explaining exactly what is living in the walls. Short, illustrated and briskly creepy, the opening of the Spiderwick books at barely a hundred pages.
book.book100.title: Five Little Peppers and How They Grew; Five Little Peppers #1
book.book100.author: Margaret Sidney Porter
book.book100.description: Five children and their widowed mother keep a cheerful house on almost nothing, and mend, scheme and sing their way through every setback. Sentimental, cosy, wholly of its century, and first of many.
book.book101.title: Five on a Treasure Island
book.book101.author: Enid Blyton
book.book101.description: Four cousins, one extremely good dog, and an island with a wrecked ship and a map nobody else has read properly. Picnics, dungeons and villains who never stood a chance. First of many summers.
book.book102.title: Five Survive
book.book102.author: Holly Jackson
book.book102.description: Six teenagers, one stranded motorhome, and a shooter out in the dark who says nobody leaves until a secret gets confessed. One night, told almost in real time, and the friend group will not survive it whole.
book.book103.title: A Florence Diary
book.book103.author: Diana Athill
book.book103.description: Eighty pages of a young Englishwoman's first Italian summer: churches, chaperones, heat and gelato, recorded on the spot. A slight, sunlit travel notebook published long after the trip it describes.
book.book104.title: Flower Fables
book.book104.author: Louisa May Alcott
book.book104.description: Flower fairies, elves and small moral errands in the woods, written to amuse one child long before her author was famous. Sweet, slight, occasionally preachy, and a curiosity worth the shelf space.
book.book105.title: Flowers for Algernon
book.book105.author: Daniel Keyes
book.book105.description: Charlie Gordon writes progress reports. The surgery that tripled a laboratory mouse's intelligence is tried on him next, and the reports change as he does. Quietly devastating science fiction about who was kind to whom.
book.book106.title: The Forests of Silence; (Deltora Quest #1)
book.book106.author: Emily Rodda
book.book106.description: Seven gems were prised from the Belt of Deltora and hidden, and a blacksmith's son sets out after the first of them. Short, brisk quest fantasy for younger readers, with a map, a riddle and a forest nobody walks out of.
book.book107.title: The Forgotten Beasts of Eld
book.book107.author: Patricia A. McKillip
book.book107.description: On a lonely mountain a wizard's daughter keeps company with legendary beasts and wants nothing at all from people, until a baby is left in her arms. Lyrical, fierce, and quietly clear about what vengeance costs.
book.book108.title: Frog and Toad Together
book.book108.author: Arnold Lobel
book.book108.description: Five small stories about two amphibian friends: a list of things to do, a garden that refuses to hurry, and a plate of cookies that must be dealt with. Sixty-four pages of perfect gentle nonsense.
book.book109.title: Full Dark, No Stars
book.book109.author: Stephen King
book.book109.description: Four novellas about ordinary people who step over a line and then have to live in the room with it: a farmer, a novelist, a bargain too good to refuse, a wife who finds something in the garage. Plain-spoken, no comfort offered.
book.book110.title: Games, Game Design, Game Studies
book.book110.author: Gundolf S. Freyermuth
book.book110.description: Where do games come from, and how did studying them become a discipline? A brisk academic primer on design practice and the young field built around it, written for students and dry in the way syllabi are.
book.book111.title: The Garden of Evening Mists
book.book111.author: Tan Twan Eng
book.book111.description: Years after a prison camp she barely survived, a retired judge goes back to a garden in the Malayan highlands and to the Japanese gardener who taught her. Slow, beautiful, withholding; secrets surface late.
book.book112.title: Gone Girl
book.book112.author: Gillian Flynn
book.book112.description: A wife vanishes on the morning of her fifth anniversary, and her husband keeps saying the wrong thing on camera. Two accounts, one marriage, and the ground shifts hard about halfway through.
book.book113.title: Good Girl, Bad Blood
book.book113.author: Holly Jackson
book.book113.description: Done with detective work and having said so publicly, Pip picks it up again when a friend's brother vanishes and the police shrug. A missing-person hunt told through her podcast, with school, guilt and growing up crowding in.
book.book114.title: Good Night, Gorilla
book.book114.author: Peggy Rathmann
book.book114.description: The zookeeper says goodnight, the gorilla lifts his keys, and the whole zoo tiptoes home to bed behind him. Almost wordless, endlessly rereadable, and small children spot the balloon before you do.
book.book116.title: A Gothic Cookbook; Hauntingly Delicious Recipes Inspired by 13 Classic Tales
book.book116.author: Ella Buchan & Dr Allesandra Pino
book.book116.description: Thirteen gothic classics, raided for supper. Recipes, menus and literary notes that let you cook your way through mist, inheritance and the odd disappearance, illustrated for readers who like their baking atmospheric.
book.book117.title: Gregor the Overlander
book.book117.author: Suzanne Collins
book.book117.description: Doing the laundry ends with an eleven-year-old and his toddler sister dropping through a grate into a subterranean world of giant bats and warring rats, where a prophecy is waiting with his name in it.
book.book118.title: Gulliver's Travels
book.book118.author: Jonathan Swift
book.book118.description: Shipwreck by shipwreck, a ship's surgeon washes up among giants, tiny warring courtiers and talking horses. Straight-faced comedy from 1726 that is really a very rude joke about governments.
book.book119.title: Hamlet
book.book119.author: William Shakespeare
book.book119.description: The ghost on the battlements names a murderer, and the prince who hears it thinks himself half to death before he moves. Still the sharpest thing ever written about grief, doubt and the price of delay.
book.book120.title: Hamnet
book.book120.author: Maggie O'Farrell
book.book120.description: Plague comes to a Warwickshire household, and the mother at its centre, herb-wise and half-feared by her neighbours, cannot keep it from her son. Grief written so closely it aches, with a play waiting after.
book.book121.title: Heartstopper; Volume 1
book.book121.author: Alice Oseman
book.book121.description: Two schoolboys get seated together in form and one of them falls hard, drawn in soft pencil with leaves tumbling across the panels. Sweet, queer, low-stakes comics, and the start of something ongoing.
book.book122.title: Heidi
book.book122.author: Johanna Spyri
book.book122.description: An orphan is handed to a gruff grandfather high in the Alps, thrives among goats and mountain air, then is carried off to a city house that cannot hold her. Warm, old-fashioned, and sure of its happy ending.
book.book123.title: The Hobbit; The Lord of the Rings #0
book.book123.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book.book123.description: Bilbo Baggins is bullied out of his comfortable hole by thirteen dwarves and a wizard with an agenda. Cosy, funny, full of songs, and the doorway to everything Middle-earth becomes later.
book.book124.title: Homage to Catalonia
book.book124.author: George Orwell
book.book124.description: A volunteer's account of the Spanish war from the trenches, and then from the wrong side of a purge. Lice, boredom, courage and betrayal, reported plainly by a man who was shot through the throat.
book.book125.title: Home Before Dark
book.book125.author: Riley Sager
book.book125.description: Her father got rich writing about the house that drove the family out in the night. The house is hers now, she is certain the book was a lie, and she has come back with tools. Chapters of that old bestseller sit between hers.
book.book126.title: Howl's Moving Castle
book.book126.author: Diana Wynne Jones
book.book126.description: Sophie makes hats and expects nothing, then a slighted witch turns her ninety. Refuge comes in a walking castle run by a vain wizard and a fire demon who bargains. Funny, warm and far cleverer than its fairy tale shape.
book.book127.title: If Not, Winter; (Fragments of Sappho)
book.book127.author: Sappho, transl. by A. Carson
book.book127.description: Every surviving scrap of Sappho, brackets and all, with the gaps left visible so the silence does its share of the work. Desire in fragments, and somehow more devastating for everything that burned away.
book.book128.title: If We Were Villains
book.book128.author: M. L. Rio
book.book128.description: Ten years served, and the actor walks out ready to tell a retired detective what really happened at the Shakespeare conservatory. Seven fourth-year students, one death, and verse doing the work of confession. Theatrical and doomed.
book.book129.title: The Illustrated Dust Jacket, 1920-1970
book.book129.author: Martin Salisbury
book.book129.description: Between the wars and after, a book's jacket was where illustrators showed off. Designer by designer, plate by plate, this survey catalogues that golden stretch of jacket art, with the text kept short and factual.
book.book130.title: In Cold Blood
book.book130.author: Truman Capote
book.book130.description: Two killers, a farmhouse in Holcomb, Kansas, and a family shot in their own beds: the reporting that followed invented a genre. Neighbours, lawmen and the long wait on death row, set down with awful calm. True crime before the term.
book.book131.title: Inferno
book.book131.author: Dante Alighieri, transl. by A. Esolen
book.book131.description: Lost in a wood at the middle of his life, a poet is handed Virgil as a guide and walks down through nine circles of punishment, each one fitted to its sin. Verse that is grisly, gossipy, and hard to shake off.
book.book132.title: The Inheritance Games
book.book132.author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
book.book132.description: Why would a billionaire leave everything to a schoolgirl he never met? To find out she has to live in his mansion with the grandsons he cut off. Riddles in the panelling, four furious heirs, and a series that enjoys withholding.
book.book133.title: It
book.book133.author: Stephen King
book.book133.description: Derry, Maine eats its children on a schedule, and seven misfits are the only ones who notice. Decades later the phone rings and they go back. Over a thousand pages of friendship, memory, and something wearing a clown suit.
book.book134.title: Italian Villas and Their Gardens
book.book134.author: Edith Wharton
book.book134.description: Villa by villa through Italy, measuring terraces, cypress walks and water stairs with an eye that cares about proportion rather than pretty flowers. Exacting, unsentimental, and a gardener's dream of an itinerary.
book.book135.title: James and the Giant Peach
book.book135.author: Roald Dahl
book.book135.description: Two horrible aunts, a handful of spilled magic, and a peach that grows bigger than a house. Inside it wait a spider, a grasshopper and a centipede, and one lonely boy finally has a family worth sailing off with.
book.book136.title: Journey to the Centre of the Earth
book.book136.author: Jules Verne
book.book136.description: Down a volcano in Iceland go a professor, his reluctant nephew and an unflappable guide, following a coded parchment toward the basement of the world. Wildly unscientific, and wildly good fun.
book.book137.title: Julie Chan is Dead
book.book137.author: Liann Zhang
book.book137.description: Her twin sister was famous, beloved online, and is now dead on the floor of a spotless apartment. Stepping into that life looks easier than explaining it. Fast, nasty satire of influencer sainthood with a body underneath.
book.book138.title: Julius Caesar
book.book138.author: William Shakespeare
book.book138.description: Honourable men talk themselves into a knife, then find that killing a ruler was the easy half. Cold, argumentative political theatre, plus the finest funeral speech ever used to turn a crowd.
book.book139.title: Jurassic Park
book.book139.author: Michael Crichton
book.book139.description: Cloned dinosaurs stock an island park, a mathematician insists the whole system is bound to fail, and then the fences go down. More biotech briefing and chaos theory than the film, and scarier for it.
book.book140.title: Kiki's Delivery Service
book.book140.author: Eiko Kadono
book.book140.description: Thirteen is the age a young witch must leave home for a year, so off she flies with a talkative black cat and one useful skill. Setting up a delivery service in a seaside town turns out to be the harder trick.
book.book141.title: King Stakh's Wild Hunt
book.book141.author: Uladzimir Karatkievich
book.book141.description: Out on the marshes a decaying manor shelters the last heiress of a cursed line, and the phantom riders of the old legend are already stirring. Belarusian gothic, thick with fog and cleverly plotted.
book.book142.title: Henry V
book.book142.author: William Shakespeare
book.book142.description: Young King Harry takes an army across the Channel and stakes a reign on a muddy field at Agincourt. A history play about the rhetoric of war and who pays for it, and part of a four-play cycle.
book.book143.title: Labyrinths
book.book143.author: Jorge Luis Borges
book.book143.description: Libraries bent into infinity, a garden that forks into every possible path, reviews of books nobody wrote. Stories, essays and parables, short and bottomless, from the great architect of the philosophical maze.
book.book144.title: Lady Audley's Secret
book.book144.author: Mary Elizabeth Braddon
book.book144.description: A golden-haired young wife has married very well, and her husband's nephew starts pulling at the thread of who she was before. Victorian sensation at full pelt: a vanished man, a well, and no quiet fainting.
book.book145.title: Le Corbusier
book.book145.author: Le Corbusier
book.book145.description: Drawings, doctrine and buildings from the hard edge of modern architecture, in a slim interwar volume that argues as much as it illustrates. Dry, specialist, and aimed at readers who already speak the language.
book.book146.title: Leave Taking
book.book146.author: Winsome Pinnock
book.book146.description: Enid left Jamaica for London years ago; her daughters were born here and want none of it. A short play about a mother, a healer and the arguments families have standing up in kitchens. Funny where it hurts.
book.book147.title: Little Women
book.book147.author: Louisa May Alcott
book.book147.description: Four sisters, one shabby house, a father away at the war: Meg wants comfort, Jo wants to write, Beth wants nobody upset, Amy wants more. Growing up happens in small scenes here, and it earns its warmth.
book.book148.title: Love
book.book148.author: Toni Morrison
book.book148.description: Two old women share a crumbling seaside house and a hatred fifty years deep, both of them shaped by the same charming hotel owner. Morrison tells it sideways, in prose that will not hurry for anyone.
book.book149.title: Macbeth
book.book149.author: William Shakespeare
book.book149.description: Three strangers on a heath tell a Scottish general he will be king, and his wife makes certain of it. The shortest tragedy Shakespeare wrote, running on blood, sleeplessness and a crown nobody enjoys.
book.book150.title: Mend! A Refashioning Manual and Manifesto
book.book150.author: Kate Sekules
book.book150.description: Darning is an argument now. Visible stitches, patches worn on purpose and a short history of mending, from a writer who would rather your wardrobe was repaired than replaced. Practical, opinionated, easy to dip into.
book.book151.title: Meridian
book.book151.author: Alice Walker
book.book151.description: Meridian Hill gives up a child, a marriage and eventually her health to the civil rights movement, then keeps working long after the marches stop. An unsparing novel about what activism asks of one body.
book.book152.title: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
book.book152.author: Howard Pyle
book.book152.description: Episode after episode of Sherwood mischief: quarterstaff duels on bridges, a disguised archer at the sheriff's contest, fat purses relieved of their owners. Mock-old English that rolls along merrily.
book.book153.title: Merry Mister Meddle; Mister Meddle Series
book.book153.author: Enid Blyton
book.book153.description: Mister Meddle cannot leave anything alone, and every attempt to be helpful ends with a pixie in disgrace and somebody's day in ruins. Short silly chapters, built for reading one at a time to a giggling child.
book.book154.title: Middlemarch
book.book154.author: George Eliot
book.book154.description: Dorothea marries a scholar for his great work and learns what it is worth; a young doctor marries for beauty and gets debt. Provincial England in patient, enormous detail, and a narrator who sees through everyone.
book.book155.title: milk and honey
book.book155.author: Rupi Kaur
book.book155.description: Four sections, the hurting, the loving, the breaking and the healing, in short unpunctuated poems with line drawings beside them. Plain words about abuse, love and getting yourself back afterwards.
book.book156.title: Misery
book.book156.author: Stephen King
book.book156.description: Waking from a crash in a stranger's spare room with his legs ruined, a novelist learns that his rescuer has read everything he ever wrote and hated how the last one ended. Two people, one typewriter, and nobody coming up the road.
book.book157.title: Moby-Dick
book.book157.author: Herman Melville
book.book157.description: Signing onto a whaler turns into a hunt for one white whale and the captain who has staked everything on finding it. Half sea story, half encyclopedia of whales, and the digressions are the point, not a detour.
book.book158.title: Momo; or, The Grey Gentlemen
book.book158.author: Michael Ende
book.book158.description: Grey gentlemen in grey hats are talking a town into saving its time, and only a girl living in a ruined amphitheatre notices what is being stolen. Fable-shaped, with a tortoise who spells out the future.
book.book159.title: Journey to the West; or, Monkey King
book.book159.author: Wu Cheng'en
book.book159.description: Press-ganged into escorting a timid monk to India for holy scriptures, a monkey who once fought heaven itself sets out with a greedy pig for company. Demons every few chapters, slapstick and sermon side by side.
book.book160.title: The Journey; Big Panda and Tiny Dragon #2
book.book160.author: James Norbury
book.book160.description: Panda and dragon take to the road again, through snow, doubt and long stretches of nothing much. Illustrated, unhurried and full of small kindnesses, it asks what to do when the path you were following disappears.
book.book161.title: Murder on the Orient Express
book.book161.author: Agatha Christie
book.book161.description: Snowdrifts halt the train somewhere in the Balkans, a passenger is found stabbed behind a bolted door, and every traveller in the carriage has a tidy alibi. The Belgian works the corridor. Famous ending, best reached cold.
book.book162.title: Night Shift
book.book162.author: Stephen King
book.book162.description: Twenty stories from King's first collection: trucks that drive themselves, a laundry press with an appetite, a Maine town that empties after dark. Nasty, efficient horror and a very good place to start.
book.book163.title: The Nightingale
book.book163.author: Hans Christian Andersen
book.book163.description: An emperor hears that the finest thing in his kingdom is a plain brown bird in the woods, then trades it for a jewelled clockwork one. Short, and clear-eyed about what a living song is worth. No scolding.
book.book164.title: Nimona
book.book164.author: N. D. Stevenson
book.book164.description: Ballister Blackheart is a supervillain with standards. Nimona is the shapeshifting sidekick who has none, and no visible bottom either. A graphic novel that is hilarious right up until it decides to break your heart.
book.book165.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
book.book165.author: George Orwell
book.book165.description: Winston Smith rewrites yesterday's newspapers for a living, and falls in love anyway. The bleakest thing on the shelf, still quoted in every argument about power, and it offers no way out.
book.book166.title: Non-Binary Lives; An Anthology of Intersecting Identities
book.book166.author: Various Authors
book.book166.description: Essays and life stories from people whose gender sits outside the binary, and who are also, variously, disabled, religious, working class or of colour. Personal, political, and told in their own voices.
book.book167.title: Normal People
book.book167.author: Sally Rooney
book.book167.description: Connell is popular at school, Marianne is not, and his mother cleans her house. From a small Irish town to Trinity College they keep finding each other and getting it wrong. Class and love, told exactly.
book.book168.title: Northanger Abbey
book.book168.author: Jane Austen
book.book168.description: Catherine Morland reads too many horrid novels, goes to Bath, and arrives at a real abbey fully prepared for murdered wives and secret passages. Austen's funniest romance, and a fond joke at gothic fiction.
book.book169.title: The Notebooks of Malte Laurids Brigge
book.book169.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
book.book169.description: Alone in Paris, a young Danish poet fills notebooks with whatever frightens him: hospitals, faces in the street, his own childhood, the ways people die. Barely a plot, and startling sentence by sentence.
book.book170.title: Notes From A Small Island
book.book170.author: Bill Bryson
book.book170.description: A farewell lap around Britain by bus and footpath, arguing with hotel breakfasts and admiring the drizzle. Fond and very rude about the same places, often in the same sentence.
book.book171.title: One Of Us Is Lying
book.book171.author: Karen M. McManus
book.book171.description: Five students walk into detention and only four walk out. Each survivor had something the dead boy was about to publish, and the whole school is delighted to speculate. Four narrators, all of them lying about something.
book.book172.title: One Piece; Volume 1
book.book172.author: Eiichiro Oda
book.book172.description: Monkey D. Luffy ate the wrong fruit, turned to rubber, and decided to become King of the Pirates regardless. First volume of an extremely long voyage: loud, daft, and far better hearted than it looks.
book.book173.title: Paper Towns
book.book173.author: John Green
book.book173.description: Margo climbs through Quentin's window for one night of revenge errands, then vanishes, leaving clues only he would notice. A road trip about the gap between a girl and the girl you decided she was.
book.book174.title: Paradise
book.book174.author: Toni Morrison
book.book174.description: Nine men from an all-Black Oklahoma town drive out to an old convent where a handful of women live alone, and they bring guns. Morrison unpicks that morning backwards, woman by woman. Demanding, and worth it.
book.book175.title: Persuasion
book.book175.author: Jane Austen
book.book175.description: Anne Elliot was persuaded out of marrying a poor sailor eight years ago. Now he is back, rich, and civil to everyone but her. Austen's quietest and most grown-up romance, with a letter worth the wait.
book.book176.title: Pet Sematary
book.book176.author: Stephen King
book.book176.description: Behind the children's pet graveyard in the Maine woods lies older ground that returns what you bury, not quite as it went in. A father learns this, then finds a reason to use it. Grief written as horror, and merciless with it.
book.book177.title: Rambles in Germany and Italy; in 1840, 1842, and 1843
book.book177.author: Mary Shelley
book.book177.description: Letters home from a widow travelling the continent with her grown son, taking in galleries, lakes, politics and her own long memories. Unhurried, particular, and far more personal than most such journals of its day.
book.book178.title: Red Dragon
book.book178.author: Thomas Harris
book.book178.description: Coaxed out of retirement, a profiler hunts a killer who works through whole families by moonlight, and the only mind that can help belongs to the man who nearly finished him. Empathy as an occupational injury. Where Lecter begins.
book.book179.title: The Red Virgin; Memoirs of Louise Michel
book.book179.author: Louise Michel
book.book179.description: Memoirs of the anarchist schoolteacher who fought for the Paris Commune, dared her judges to shoot her, and kept organising from a penal colony. Dense, partisan, and not much interested in charming anyone.
book.book180.title: Red, White & Royal Blue
book.book180.author: Casey McQuiston
book.book180.description: The First Son of the United States and a prince of England wreck a royal wedding cake, then have to fake a friendship for the cameras. Emails, borrowed hotel rooms and an election at stake. Very funny.
book.book181.title: Redwall; Book 1
book.book181.author: Brian Jacques
book.book181.description: Cluny the Scourge has designs on Redwall Abbey, and the mice inside have a legend and one clumsy novice to work with. Animal adventure with siege warfare, riddles, and feasts described in indecent detail.
book.book182.title: Richard Serra; Interviews, etc., 1970-1980
book.book182.author: Richard Serra
book.book182.description: A sculptor talks shop across a decade: steel, weight, site, process, and what happens when a work refuses to be moved. Interviews rather than a life story, dense throughout, and best suited to art-school shelves.
book.book183.title: Romancero Gitano
book.book183.author: Federico García Lorca
book.book183.description: Andalusian ballads where the moon walks into a forge, knives find ribs, and the civil guard rides in black. Slim, incantatory, colours used as omens; read them aloud even if the Spanish is out of reach.
book.book184.title: Romeo and Juliet
book.book184.author: William Shakespeare
book.book184.description: Two teenagers from feuding Verona households meet at a party and marry in secret inside a day, helped along by a friar, a nurse and a street brawl. A tragedy of pure speed, with nobody old enough to slow it.
book.book185.title: Salomé
book.book185.author: Oscar Wilde
book.book185.description: Herod's stepdaughter wants the imprisoned prophet to look at her, and when he will not, she names her price for a dance. A one-act tragedy of moonlight, obsession and lines that repeat like an incantation.
book.book186.title: Saving Danny
book.book186.author: Cathy Glass
book.book186.description: A five-year-old autistic boy arrives at a foster carer's door frightened, furious and asking after his dog. The carer tells it herself, plainly, and is kinder than you expect about parents out of their depth.
book.book187.title: The Saviour Fish; Life and Death on Africa's Greatest Lake
book.book187.author: Mark Weston
book.book187.description: One introduced fish made fortunes and unmade a lake. Reported from an island where the catch keeps shrinking, this is patient, unsparing writing about ecology, poverty and politics on the water. Not a cheerful trip.
book.book188.title: Second Foundation
book.book188.author: Isaac Asimov
book.book188.description: Third in the Foundation sequence. A second, secret order of mind-shapers is supposed to be steering history from somewhere, and half the galaxy wants its address. Asimov at his most puzzle-like, and barely a doorstop.
book.book189.title: Shakespeare; The World as Stage
book.book189.author: Bill Bryson
book.book189.description: How much can actually be known about the man from Stratford? Very little, it turns out, and the hunt for it is the fun. A short, funny, sceptical biography that prefers evidence to legend.
book.book190.title: Shatter Me
book.book190.author: Tahereh Mafi
book.book190.description: Juliette's touch kills, which is why she was locked away and why the regime now wants her back. Dystopian YA in feverish, crossed-out prose, all first love and worse decisions. The opening of a long series.
book.book191.title: Shearwater; A Bird, an Ocean, and a Long Way Home
book.book191.author: Roger Morgan-Grenville
book.book191.description: Few birds travel like the shearwater, and following one across oceans turns into a reckoning with home, friendship and getting older. Nature writing with salt in it: curious, companionable, quietly enormous.
book.book192.title: Shirley
book.book192.author: Charlotte Brontë
book.book192.description: Yorkshire mill workers smash the new machines while two very different women, a shy curate's niece and an heiress who signs herself like a man, work out what they want. Long, argumentative, and no mere romance.
book.book193.title: Six of Crows
book.book193.author: Leigh Bardugo
book.book193.description: Six criminals, one fortress nobody has ever broken into, and a payday big enough to make the odds look survivable. Heist fantasy with a razor of a crew, a drug that breaks magic, and Ketterdam's filthy charm.
book.book194.title: Sky Island
book.book194.author: L. Frank Baum
book.book194.description: Two children and an old sailor lift off under a magic umbrella and land clean off the map, on an island split between a blue half and a pink half that cannot abide each other. Sunny, silly nonsense throughout.
book.book195.title: Skyward; (Book 1)
book.book195.author: Brandon Sanderson
book.book195.description: Spensa wants to fly, and the people who call her father a coward have no intention of letting her. Humanity underground, alien raids, and a sarcastic ship buried in the hills. Hopeful, propulsive space opera.
book.book196.title: Slaughterhouse-Five
book.book196.author: Kurt Vonnegut
book.book196.description: Billy Pilgrim comes unstuck in time, bouncing between a prisoner-of-war cellar under Dresden, a dull suburban marriage, and a zoo on another planet. Jokes and atrocity in one sentence, and a shrug that never lifts.
book.book197.title: Small Spaces; (Book 1)
book.book197.author: Katherine Arden
book.book197.description: The school bus stalls in the fog on the way back from a farm, the scarecrows in the fields have moved, and a stopped watch spells out advice: keep to small spaces. Genuinely frightening, and only the first.
book.book198.title: Snow Crash
book.book198.author: Neal Stephenson
book.book198.description: A pizza courier for the Mafia moonlights as the best swordsman in the Metaverse, then a drug that infects hackers and their brains alike starts spreading. Cyberpunk satire, loud, funny, and built on Sumerian grammar.
book.book199.title: Stories of Your Life and Others
book.book199.author: Ted Chiang
book.book199.description: Eight stories, each taking one idea entirely seriously: a language that unsticks time, a tower built to reach heaven, a world where angel visits leave wreckage. Cool, precise science fiction that earns its sadness.
book.book200.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
book.book200.author: John Green
book.book200.description: Rating the human-shaped planet on a five-star scale, one small subject at a time, from sunsets to soft drinks. Essays that start funny and land somewhere tender, with a scientist's curiosity and a fan's warmth.
book.book201.title: Antigone
book.book201.author: Sophocles
book.book201.description: Her brother lies unburied outside the walls by order of the king, and Antigone decides the gods outrank him. Eighty pages of Greek tragedy setting law against conscience, still argued over in every seminar.
book.book202.title: Antony and Cleopatra
book.book202.author: William Shakespeare
book.book202.description: A Roman general who is meant to be running half an empire cannot make himself leave Egypt, or its queen. Late Shakespeare, moving between marble and barge, with no mercy at all for middle-aged love.
book.book203.title: Anxious People
book.book203.author: Fredrik Backman
book.book203.description: A bank robbery goes wrong and the robber ends up holding an apartment viewing hostage, which turns out to be eight strangers who badly needed an excuse to talk. Warm, funny, far more curious about people than about the crime.
book.book204.title: The Autograph Man
book.book204.author: Zadie Smith
book.book204.description: Alex-Li Tandem buys and sells other people's signatures, chases one reclusive actress, and keeps not saying kaddish for his father. A comic London novel about fame, faith, and avoiding the thing in front of you.
book.book205.title: The Bad Beginning; (A Series of Unfortunate Events)
book.book205.author: Lemony Snicket
book.book205.description: Three clever orphans, one enormous fortune, and a guardian with a single eyebrow and theatrical ambitions. The narrator warns you off every few pages, which is of course why the next twelve books exist.
book.book206.title: Bait and Witch; (Witch Way Librarian Mysteries #1)
book.book206.author: Angela M. Sanders
book.book206.description: Exiled to a tiny Oregon town after saying the wrong thing in Washington, a librarian discovers the books whisper to her and that someone in the woods has died. Cosy magic, small-town suspicion, and the start of a series.
book.book207.title: Baking with Kim-Joy; Cute and Creative Bakes to Make You Smile
book.book207.author: Kim-Joy
book.book207.description: Bakes with faces. Animals piped, iced and assembled step by step, in a decorating book for home bakers who would like their kitchen cheerful rather than serious. Cute is the whole point here, and it works.
book.book208.title: The Ballad of Jacquotte Delahaye
book.book208.author: Briony Cameron
book.book208.description: Jacquotte Delahaye loses her father and his shipyard, and takes to the Caribbean under her own flag. A debut novel that turns a half-legendary pirate into a woman with a crew, a temper and a love of her own.
book.book209.title: The Bar Code Tattoo; (Bar Code #1)
book.book209.author: Suzane Weyn
book.book209.description: At seventeen the tattoo becomes compulsory, a barcode carrying everything about you, including what your genes are said to predict. Kayla refuses. Short, blunt dystopian YA about data as destiny.
book.book210.title: Barmy British Empire; Horrible Histories
book.book210.author: Terry Deary
book.book210.description: History for children with the gruesome bits left in: empire, plunder, disease and some truly poor decisions, told in jokes, cartoons and lists. Part of a long series that turned squeamish readers into history fans.
book.book211.title: Baroque
book.book211.author: John Rupert Martin
book.book211.description: Illusion, naturalism, allegory, light: baroque art sorted by idea rather than by date, across painting, sculpture and the buildings that framed them. A compact survey with plates, clear enough for beginners.
book.book212.title: The Battle of the Labyrinth
book.book212.author: Rick Riordan
book.book212.description: Fourth Percy Jackson book, and the war finally reaches camp. The way in runs through Daedalus's Labyrinth, which rearranges itself and resists being mapped. Funny, quick, and heavier than the ones before it.
book.book213.title: Battle Royale
book.book213.author: Koushun Takami
book.book213.description: Ninth-graders wake on an island wearing metal collars, with orders to kill one another until one is left. Forty-two classmates, three days, and a government that files the whole thing as research. Long, brutal, and relentless.
book.book214.title: Beartown; Book 1
book.book214.author: Fredrik Backman
book.book214.description: A dying forest town pins everything on its junior ice hockey team. After the semi-final, a star player rapes the general manager's teenage daughter, and the town decides which of them to believe. First of a trilogy.
book.book215.title: The Bell Jar
book.book215.author: Sylvia Plath
book.book215.description: Esther Greenwood wins a month at a New York magazine and feels nothing at all. Her slide into breakdown, and the hospitals afterwards, set down with a clarity that never once asks for pity. Plath's only novel.
book.book216.title: The Big Sleep
book.book216.author: Raymond Chandler
book.book216.description: Blackmail is the job a dying general hires the private eye for, and it opens onto every rotten thing his daughters have touched. Los Angeles in the rain, a plot knotted past untying, and sentences worth every bit of the trouble.
book.book217.title: The Binding
book.book217.author: Bridget Collins
book.book217.description: Bookbinders take a memory out of you and bind it into a volume, and then you are free of it. Apprenticed to one, Emmett finds a book with his own name on the spine. Quiet, gorgeous fantasy with a love story underneath.
book.book218.title: Binti; (Book 1)
book.book218.author: Nnedi Okorafor
book.book218.description: Binti is the first of her people offered a place at the finest university in the galaxy, so she runs for the shuttle without telling her family. Then something boards the ship. Ninety fast pages.
book.book219.title: Bird by Bird; Some Instructions on Writing and Life
book.book219.author: Anne Lamott
book.book219.description: Stuck at page one? Permission to write a terrible first draft, then another, offered through a writing teacher's own false starts and small victories. Warm, funny, and the most quoted advice book on the craft.
book.book220.title: Birdland
book.book220.author: Simon Stephens
book.book220.description: Paul is a rock star in the last week of a world tour, and money has stopped meaning anything to him, other people included. A short contemporary play watching a man corrode hotel room by hotel room.
book.book221.title: Bleak House
book.book221.author: Charles Dickens
book.book221.description: Fog, and a lawsuit that has outlived its litigants, while a great lady's past comes up the drive and a police inspector starts asking questions. Vast, furious at the courts, and ancestor to every detective novel written since.
book.book222.title: The Blind Assassin
book.book222.author: Margaret Atwood
book.book222.description: An old woman in Ontario writes down what happened to her sister, who drove off a bridge a week after the war ended. Inside her account sits a pulp romance, and inside that, a blind killer on another planet.
book.book223.title: Blithe Spirit
book.book223.author: Noel Coward
book.book223.description: A novelist invites a medium to dinner for research and gets his first wife back: dead, visible only to him, and rude about the second one. A three-act comedy written in wartime and still genuinely funny.
book.book224.title: The Bluest Eye
book.book224.author: Toni Morrison
book.book224.description: Pecola Breedlove prays for blue eyes, certain they would make her lovable. Morrison's first novel, set in an Ohio town, follows a Black girl raped by her father and failed by every neighbour who could have helped.
book.book225.title: Blurb Your Enthusiasm: A Cracking Compendium of Book Blurbs, Writing Tips, Literary Folklore and Publishing Secrets
book.book225.author: Louise Willder
book.book225.description: Who writes the words on the back of a book, and why do they work? A copywriter's cheerful tour of blurbs, cover lines, publishing lore and the tricks that shift stock. Best read in a bookshop, out loud.
book.book226.title: Body in the Library; Miss Marple  #2
book.book226.author: Agatha Christie
book.book226.description: Found strangled on the hearthrug of a colonel's library: one blonde stranger, extremely awkward for everybody. An elderly village lady asks the questions nobody else thinks of. Fair clues, and a tidy trap.
book.book227.title: Book of Azrael
book.book227.author: Amber V Nicole
book.book227.description: Dark romantic fantasy, nearly five hundred pages of gods, bargains and monsters, written squarely for adult readers. Expect a slow burn, a high body count and a series that is nowhere near finished.
book.book229.title: The Canterville Ghost
book.book229.author: Oscar Wilde
book.book229.description: An American family buys an English manor and refuses to be frightened by the resident spectre, who takes it badly. Ninety-odd pages of impeccable mischief with a surprisingly tender ending.
book.book230.title: Caps for Sale; A Tale of a Peddler, Some Monkeys and Their Monkey Business
book.book230.author: Esphyr Slobodkina
book.book230.description: Caps stacked high on one peddler's head, a nap under a tree, and a treeful of monkeys who help themselves. Toddlers will be shouting the repeated lines back at you before the third page is turned.
book.book231.title: The Cask of Amontillado
book.book231.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book.book231.description: An insult demands payment, and the man who received it has been patient about the arrangements. Carnival overhead, damp catacombs below, a rare sherry promised at the end of the passage. Barely thirty pages of smiling malice.
book.book232.title: The Color Purple
book.book232.author: Alice Walker
book.book232.description: Celie writes letters because there is nobody safe to talk to: about a husband who breaks her, a sister sent far away, and a blues singer who teaches her she is worth something. Brutal early, then it opens up.
book.book233.title: The Colour of Magic; Discworld #1, Rincewind #1
book.book233.author: Terry Pratchett
book.book233.description: Discworld starts here, riding four elephants on the back of a turtle, with an inept wizard and the first tourist the place has ever seen. Comic fantasy still finding its feet, and already very funny indeed.
book.book234.title: The Comedy of Errors
book.book234.author: William Shakespeare
book.book234.description: Two sets of identical twins, separated at sea and all four in Ephesus on the same day with nobody told. The shortest, silliest play in the canon: wrong doors, wrong wife, and a beating for everybody.
book.book235.title: The Comfort Book
book.book235.author: Matt Haig
book.book235.description: Short notes, lists and fragments written for bad days, meant to be opened anywhere rather than read straight through. Gentle, plain-spoken comfort from someone who has needed it, and no promise that you are fixed.
book.book236.title: The Complete Father Brown
book.book236.author: G.K. Chesterton
book.book236.description: Dozens of short puzzles solved by a shabby little priest with an umbrella, who knows exactly what people do because he has spent a lifetime hearing confessions. All paradox, best taken a few at a time.
book.book237.title: The Complete Illustrated Encyclopedia of Birds of the World; A Detailed Visual Reference Guide To 1600 Birds And Their Habitats, Shown In More Than 1800 Pictures
book.book237.author: David Alderton
book.book237.description: Sixteen hundred species and more than eighteen hundred pictures, arranged by the habitats they belong to. A heavy, handsome reference to keep near the window, for birdwatchers who look things up rather than read on.
book.book238.title: The Complete Peanuts; 1993-1994
book.book238.author: Charles M. Schultz
book.book238.description: Two full years of daily and Sunday strips: Charlie Brown losing with dignity, Snoopy on the doghouse roof, and jokes about despair aimed squarely at children. Comfort reading that was always sadder than it looked.
book.book239.title: The Complete Robot
book.book239.author: Isaac Asimov
book.book239.description: Thirty-one stories about machines built to obey three laws, and the engineers, psychologists and detectives who keep finding the gaps. Asimov's robot fiction gathered whole, cool-headed and endlessly logical.
book.book240.title: The Crucible
book.book240.author: Arthur Miller
book.book240.description: Salem hangs on the word of a teenage girl, and a courtroom turns neighbour against neighbour until confessing to witchcraft is the only way to stay alive. Miller's stage tragedy about panic wearing the robes of law.
book.book241.title: The Cruel Prince
book.book241.author: Holly Black
book.book241.description: Jude is mortal, raised in Faerie by the man who murdered her parents, and she wants a place at a court that despises her for existing. Cruel, courtly YA fantasy where everyone lies beautifully. First of a trilogy.
book.book242.title: Crying in H Mart
book.book242.author: Michelle Zauner
book.book242.description: Grief tastes like the food a mother used to make. A memoir of losing her, of Korean groceries and half-belonging, and of learning the recipes far too late. Tender, exact, and unsparing about what goes unsaid.
book.book243.title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
book.book243.author: Mark Haddon
book.book243.description: Somebody has killed the neighbour's dog with a garden fork, so the fifteen-year-old who finds it opens an investigation, Holmes-fashion. Prime numbers for chapter headings, and a narrator constitutionally unable to lie.
book.book244.title: Cyrano de Bergerac
book.book244.author: Edmond Rostand
book.book244.description: Swordsman, poet, and owner of a truly magnificent nose, Cyrano lends his words to a handsomer man so that Roxane may be wooed properly. A verse play that is gloriously funny for four acts and then quietly breaks you.
book.book245.title: The Decoration of Houses
book.book245.author: Edith Wharton
book.book245.description: Clutter is the enemy; proportion is the cure. An argument for rooms planned like architecture instead of padded like parlours, with practical chapters on doors, walls and light. Opinionated, and still useful.
book.book246.title: The Dispossessed
book.book246.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
book.book246.description: Shevek leaves the anarchist moon that raised him to publish his physics on the wealthy world below, and finds both societies wanting. Science fiction as political argument: dry, humane, and still unanswered.
book.book247.title: The Duke and I
book.book247.author: Julia Quinn
book.book247.description: Daphne Bridgerton and a duke with no intention of marrying anyone stage a fake courtship to get the gossips off their backs. Regency romance, first of the Bridgerton run, frothy and headed exactly where you hope.
book.book248.title: The Essential Rumi
book.book248.author: Rumi, transl. by Barks & Moyne
book.book248.description: Sufi poems of longing dressed up as drinking songs, full of reed flutes and tavern talk, where the beloved might be God and might not. Loose, singable renderings rather than scholarly ones, made for dipping.
book.book249.title: Eugene Onegin
book.book249.author: Alexander Pushkin
book.book249.description: Bored in St Petersburg, a dandy turns down a country girl's letter, shoots his only friend in a duel over nothing, and meets her again far too late. A whole novel in rhymed stanzas, gossipy and quick.
book.book250.title: Europe Through the Back Door; A Travel Skills Handbook
book.book250.author: Rick Steves
book.book250.description: Skip the front door. Packing light, sleeping cheap, reading timetables and finding the village the tour buses miss, in a fat handbook of travel skills followed by country notes. Of its era, and still shrewd.
book.book251.title: Eurydice
book.book251.author: Sarah Ruhl
book.book251.description: The myth belongs to Eurydice here: newly dead, she meets in the underworld the father who has been waiting to teach her words again, while Orpheus plays above. A short, dreamlike stage poem about grief.
book.book252.title: Evelina
book.book252.author: Frances Burney
book.book252.description: Letters home from a country girl turned loose on London society, where every assembly is a minefield of wrong dresses and dreadful relatives. Sharp comedy of manners, courtship running underneath.
book.book253.title: Eye of the Storm; (Reel Magic Series)
book.book253.author: Meridwen Tidewell
book.book253.description: After a wild storm haunts Bookstonbury's shores, four adventurous kids find a mischievous mermaid by an old shipwreck. Sneaking kelp tea and dodging nosy adults, they decode slippery clues to help her uncover something fishy hidden beneath the waves.
book.book254.title: The Eyes of Darkness
book.book254.author: Dean Koontz
book.book254.description: One year after burying her son, a Las Vegas producer starts finding messages insisting he is not dead. Grief, a cruel hoax, or something worse behind a government fence in the mountains. Brisk, paranoid, built for one sitting.
book.book255.title: The Fall of the House of Usher
book.book255.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book.book255.description: Invited to a crumbling house that appears to be ill along with its owner, a visitor finds Roderick Usher nerve-flayed and his sister fading. Dread as architecture, and this edition pads the doom out with more tales and verse.
book.book256.title: Famous Last Words
book.book256.author: Gillian McAllister
book.book256.description: An ordinary morning ends with her husband named on the news as a hostage-taker, leaving behind a note she cannot read straight. Years of not knowing, a negotiator who never let go, and a reason that keeps shifting shape.
book.book257.title: The Fault in Our Stars
book.book257.author: John Green
