book.book257.description: Hazel has thyroid cancer and a favourite novel with no ending. Augustus has one leg and a great deal of nerve. They fly to Amsterdam to ask an author a question. Funny right up until the moment it is not.
book.book258.title: The Glass Castle
book.book258.author: Jeannette Walls
book.book258.description: Four children raised on charm, hunger and a father's blueprints for a house he never built, moving town whenever the rent came due. A memoir clear-eyed about the cost and unwilling to hate anyone for it.
book.book259.title: The God of Small Things
book.book259.author: Arundhati Roy
book.book259.description: Twins in Kerala grow up among pickle vats, a river and a family rule about who may be loved and how much. Roy circles one afternoon that broke everything, told in a child's dazzling, sideways English.
book.book260.title: The Great Gatsby
book.book260.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
book.book260.description: Next door, a man throws enormous parties for strangers, hoping that one night the woman across the bay will walk in. Told by a neighbour who half admires him; short, glittering, colder than the parties look.
book.book261.title: The Handmaid's Tale
book.book261.author: Margaret Atwood
book.book261.description: Gilead has solved its fertility crisis by assigning fertile women to powerful men, and Offred remembers the country it replaced. Cold, careful prose that still notices small pleasures. Harrowing, and hard to argue with.
book.book262.title: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
book.book262.author: Oscar Wilde
book.book262.description: Piece by piece, a gilded statue and the swallow who stayed too late in the season give away everything they have. Five short fairy tales, sharp-witted on the surface and quietly heartbreaking underneath.
book.book263.title: Hard Times
book.book263.author: Charles Dickens
book.book263.description: In a smoke-blackened mill town a schoolmaster raises his children on facts and nothing else, and his daughter's marriage is the bill for it. Angry, very funny about the pompous, and short for what it is.
book.book264.title: Hatchet
book.book264.author: Gary Paulsen
book.book264.description: The pilot dies mid-flight and a thirteen-year-old puts the little plane down in a Canadian lake with nothing useful but the hatchet on his belt. Fire, fish, a moose, and the slow arithmetic of staying alive.
book.book265.title: The Hidden Staircase; (Nancy Drew #2)
book.book265.author: Carolyn Keene
book.book265.description: Two elderly sisters report creaking floors, odd music and vanishing valuables in their old mansion, so the teenage detective packs a bag and goes looking for the passage behind it all. Brisk, tidy, vintage.
book.book266.title: The Hunger Games
book.book266.author: Suzanne Collins
book.book266.description: Twelve districts, two children each, one televised arena, and Katniss volunteering to spare her sister. Narrated in a present tense that never lets up. Dystopian YA that reshaped an entire shelf.
book.book267.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
book.book267.author: Oscar Wilde
book.book267.description: Two men invent imaginary relatives to escape their obligations, then propose to two women under the same borrowed name. Wilde's comedy of manners runs on epigrams alone, and the cucumber sandwiches do not survive.
book.book268.title: The Invasion; (Animorphs #1)
book.book268.author: K. A. Applegate
book.book268.description: A shortcut across a construction site puts five kids in front of a dying alien, who hands them the power to become any animal they touch. The parasites already walking among them will not expect a hawk.
book.book269.title: The Invention of Hugo Cabret
book.book269.author: Brian Selznick
book.book269.description: An orphan winds the clocks of a Paris station, steals parts for a broken automaton, and stumbles onto a filmmaker everyone forgot. Half the story is told in pencil drawings, and the pages fly.
book.book270.title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
book.book270.author: V.E. Schwab
book.book270.description: Bargain with a power in the dark and you get forever, but nobody will remember your name. Three centuries of being forgotten, until one man says he does. Tender, aching, and honest about what it costs to leave no mark.
book.book271.title: The Invisible Man
book.book271.author: H. G. Wells
book.book271.description: Griffin cracks the optics of the human body and turns himself transparent, then finds no way back. A bandaged stranger at a village inn becomes a study in what a man does once nobody can watch him.
book.book272.title: Is a River Alive
book.book272.author: Robert MacFarlane
book.book272.description: Can a river hold rights of its own? Journeys to three threatened waterways, among lawyers, activists and people who speak of rivers as kin, in nature writing that is lyrical and pointedly political at once.
book.book273.title: The Island of Missing Trees
book.book273.author: Elif Shafak
book.book273.description: A Greek Cypriot boy and a Turkish Cypriot girl meet in a Nicosia tavern with a fig tree growing through its roof. Decades later that tree, replanted in a London garden, tells their daughter what the war cost.
book.book274.title: The Last Battle; (Chronicles of Narnia)
book.book274.author: C.S. Lewis
book.book274.description: A cunning ape dresses a donkey in a lion skin, and Narnia believes him. The seventh and final chronicle, where the talking beasts must choose sides and the country everyone loved comes to its last morning.
book.book275.title: The Last Time I Lied
book.book275.author: Riley Sager
book.book275.description: Three girls walked out of their cabin one night at summer camp and never came back. The one left behind has spent fifteen years painting them, and now the camp reopens and she takes the job. Lake, woods, Two Truths and a Lie.
book.book276.title: The Last Wish; (The Witcher)
book.book276.author: Andrzej Sapkowski
book.book276.description: Geralt of Rivia kills monsters for coin, and the monsters are rarely the worst thing in the room. Short stories that take old folk tales, strip the moral off and leave the blood. Where the Witcher saga starts.
book.book277.title: Life is Better When You Draw It
book.book277.author: Koosje Koene
book.book277.description: Ten minutes and a pen is enough to start. Prompts, exercises and hand-drawn encouragement for people convinced they cannot draw, arranged so you can open anywhere and put a mark on paper today.
book.book278.title: The Lighthouse Mystery; The Boxcar Children #8
book.book278.author: Gertrude Chandler Warner
book.book278.description: Summer in a cottage beside a working lighthouse, and the Alden children start noticing what the grown-ups have not: odd lights, odd noises, a stray in need of feeding. Tidy, gentle detective work, finished in an afternoon.
book.book279.title: The Lightning Thief; (Percy Jackson #1)
book.book279.author: Rick Riordan
book.book279.description: Twelve years old, dyslexic, expelled again, and now Olympus says he stole Zeus's master bolt. Percy learns who his father really is and crosses America to clear his name. Greek myth with a wisecracking grin.
book.book280.title: Little Lord Fauntleroy
book.book280.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
book.book280.description: Heir to an English earldom out of nowhere, a sunny American boy goes to live with a grandfather nobody likes, cheerfully assuming the best of him. Sentimental to a fault, and it wins you over anyway.
book.book281.title: The Little Prince
book.book281.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
book.book281.description: Stranded in the desert, a pilot meets a small traveller who has left his planet and his one rose behind and is working his way from world to world. A fox explains love to him, and the ending does not soften it.
book.book282.title: The Lorax
book.book282.author: Dr. Seuss
book.book282.description: Truffula trees fall, smog rises, and a small mossy creature speaks for the trees while nobody listens. Bouncing rhyme and invented words carrying a blunt lesson about what a factory does to a forest.
book.book283.title: The Lost Symbol
book.book283.author: Dan Brown
book.book283.description: Summoned to Washington to give a lecture, the symbologist arrives to find his mentor taken and a Masonic riddle pinned to the ransom. Capitol crypts, a tattooed fanatic, one very long night of chases and impromptu seminars.
book.book284.title: The Lost Words; A Spell Book
book.book284.author: Robert Macfarlane & Jackie Morris
book.book284.description: Words that fell out of a children's dictionary, summoned back as acrostic spells and huge painted plates. Read them aloud and otter, acorn and magpie come back into the room. For any age, and quietly urgent.
book.book285.title: The Love Hypothesis
book.book285.author: Ali Hazelwood
book.book285.description: Olive kisses the nearest available man to sell a lie to her best friend, and the nearest available man turns out to be the department's most feared professor. Fake dating in a lab, with a guaranteed soft landing.
book.book286.title: Lysistrata
book.book286.author: Aristophanes
book.book286.description: Fed up with a war that never ends, the women of Greece seize the treasury and refuse their husbands until the men sit down and negotiate. Filthier than its school reputation allows, and it still plays.
book.book288.title: Madeline
book.book288.author: Ludwig Bemelmans
book.book288.description: Twelve little girls walk Paris in two straight lines, and the smallest is afraid of nothing, right up to the night she wakes with a pain and is carried off to hospital. Rhymes and loose ink drawings of the city.
book.book289.title: The Magic City
book.book289.author: Edith Nesbit
book.book289.description: Philip builds a city out of books, dominoes and silver candlesticks, then wakes to find it life-sized with himself inside it, cast as its prophesied deliverer. Edwardian nursery magic that takes its own rules seriously.
book.book290.title: The Magic World
book.book290.author: Edith Nesbit
book.book290.description: Twelve short tales in which a boy who torments the family cat wakes up inside it, a princess is betrothed to a hedgehog, and wishing reliably goes sideways. Light, brisk, and full of animals with firm opinions.
book.book291.title: The Maid; Molly the Maid #1
book.book291.author: Nita Prose
book.book291.description: Molly cleans hotel suites to a standard nobody asked for, reads people badly, and finds a wealthy guest extremely dead in his bed. Suspicion lands on whoever touched everything. Funny, kind, and a proper puzzle underneath.
book.book292.title: The Martian Chronicles
book.book292.author: Ray Bradbury
book.book292.description: Rocket after rocket leaves an Earth running out of patience with itself, and Mars answers with dry canals, gold-eyed ghosts and dust. Linked stories, more elegy than adventure, about settlers who pack their ruin with them.
book.book293.title: The Martian
book.book293.author: Andy Weir
book.book293.description: Left for dead on Mars with a punctured suit, a few potatoes and a habitat rated for thirty days, Mark Watney does the arithmetic and refuses to die. Hard science fiction that is genuinely funny about duct tape.
book.book294.title: The Massacre of Mankind
book.book294.author: Stephen Baxter
book.book294.description: The Martians came once, learned from it, and are coming back better prepared. An authorized sequel to Wells, set in an alternate Britain hardened by the first invasion, where the second is fought on a planetary scale.
book.book295.title: Maybe You Should Take to Someone; A Therapist, Her Therapist, and Our Lives Revealed
book.book295.author: Lori Gottlieb
book.book295.description: A therapist's patients arrive in crisis; so, it turns out, does she. Sessions from both sides of the couch, written with jokes and real tenderness, and more useful about ordinary unhappiness than most self-help.
book.book296.title: The Maze Runner
book.book296.author: James Dashner
book.book296.description: Thomas arrives in a metal lift with his memory wiped, into a walled Glade full of boys and a stone maze that rearranges itself every night. Runners map it, something inside hunts them, and nobody will say why.
book.book297.title: The Murder at the Vicarage
book.book297.author: Agatha Christie
book.book297.description: The least-liked man in St Mary Mead is shot in the vicar's study, and half the village would take credit. Enter an elderly spinster who gardens, listens, and is never wrong. Village crime's sharpest knitter, making her debut.
book.book298.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd (Hercule Poirot Series)
book.book298.author: Agatha Christie
book.book298.description: Village gossip about a widow's death turns serious when the squire of King's Abbot is found stabbed behind a locked door. The retired Belgian next door sets down his marrows. The most argued-over solution in crime, and it plays fair.
book.book299.title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
book.book299.author: Agatha Christie
book.book299.description: The mistress of Styles Court dies of strychnine in a house full of relatives who all stood to gain, and the little Belgian refugee in the village turns out to have been a policeman. Where Poirot starts, with the war still on.
book.book300.title: The Mysterious Benedict Society; The Mysterious Benedict Society #1
book.book300.author: Trenton Lee Stewart
book.book300.description: Answer an odd little newspaper advert, pass some very strange tests, and four gifted children find themselves sent undercover into a boarding school that is broadcasting something at the world. Codes, gadgets and proper villainy.
book.book301.title: The Namesake
book.book301.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
book.book301.description: Named in a hurry after a Russian writer his father loves for reasons he will not explain, Gogol Ganguli spends years trying to shed it. Lahiri's novel of a Bengali family building an American life in instalments.
book.book302.title: Nana; Volume 1
book.book302.author: Ai Yazawa
book.book302.description: Two women named Nana share a train to Tokyo and then an apartment: one chasing a punk band, one chasing a boyfriend. Volume one of Yazawa's manga, where the friendship is the love story and it already aches.
book.book303.title: The Napoleon of Notting Hill
book.book303.author: Gilbert K. Chesterton
book.book303.description: A bored king revives medieval pageantry for London's boroughs as a practical joke, and one young man from Notting Hill takes it entirely seriously, to the point of war. Satire with a straight face and a real sword.
book.book304.title: Nation
book.book304.author: Terry Pratchett
book.book304.description: A wave takes Mau's island and everyone on it. A wrecked ship leaves a governor's daughter on the same beach. Pratchett's standalone about two survivors rebuilding a nation and arguing, politely, with the gods.
book.book305.title: Nature; Encyclopedia of Discovery
book.book305.author: Various Authors
book.book305.description: Big pages, bigger pictures: habitats, creatures and how the living world fits together, in a nature reference built for curious young readers to browse rather than finish. Heavy enough to flatten a bookmark.
book.book306.title: The Neverending Story
book.book306.author: Michael Ende
book.book306.description: Hiding in a school attic with a stolen book, a bullied boy finds the world inside it being eaten by Nothing. Long, strange and layered, with a second half about getting every wish you ever asked for.
book.book307.title: Nevermoor; The Trials of Morrigan Crow (Nevermoor #1)
book.book307.author: Jessica Townsend
book.book307.description: Morrigan Crow is blamed for every mishap in town and due to die at midnight, until a red-haired stranger smuggles her into a hidden city and enters her in four impossible trials. Charming, inventive and generously long.
book.book308.title: The New Encyclopedia of British, European & African Birds
book.book308.author: David Alderton
book.book308.description: Species accounts and plates covering birds of Britain, Europe and Africa, arranged for looking up rather than reading through. Dry, thorough, and exactly what a birder wants in the rucksack or on the shelf.
book.book309.title: New Hampshire
book.book309.author: Robert Frost
book.book309.description: Stone walls, birches, a horse stopped beside dark woods full of snow: plain New England talk that turns unsettling if you sit with it. A long rambling title poem, then the short pieces everybody quotes.
book.book310.title: The Outsiders
book.book310.author: S. E. Hinton
book.book310.description: Ponyboy is a greaser, which in this town settles who jumps you and whom the police believe. Hinton wrote this coming-of-age novel while still a teenager herself, and the loyalty and the loss both land hard.
book.book311.title: The Passage
book.book311.author: Justin Cronin
book.book311.description: Sign the waiver and you walk off death row into a laboratory. The virus meant to make soldiers unkillable gets out and takes the continent. Nine hundred pages that open as a thriller and end a century later in a colony afraid of the dark.
book.book312.title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
book.book312.author: Stephen Chbosky
book.book312.description: Charlie writes letters to a stranger about his first year of high school, the two seniors who adopt him, and the things he cannot quite bring himself to remember. Tender, funny, and heavier than it first lets on.
book.book313.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
book.book313.author: Oscar Wilde
book.book313.description: Handed the wish that his portrait should take the damage instead of him, a beautiful young man spends years finding out how much damage he can do. Epigrams by the dozen, and real rot under the wit.
book.book314.title: A Place to Hang the Moon
book.book314.author: Kate Albus
book.book314.description: Three orphaned siblings are evacuated out of wartime London with a private plan: find not simply a billet but somebody to keep them. Book-loving, warm-hearted, and headed exactly where you hope it is headed.
book.book315.title: The Poems of Emily Dickinson; Volume II
book.book315.author: Emily Dickinson
book.book315.description: Short poems with long silences: slant rhymes, bees, a civil call paid by Death. A second gathering of Dickinson's verse, published after her death, where the plainest four lines carry the largest questions.
book.book316.title: The Ramayana
book.book316.author: Valmiki
book.book316.description: Rama is exiled on the eve of his crowning, his wife is carried off by a ten-headed king, and an army of monkeys builds a bridge to reach her. Ancient verse that still gives half of South Asia the shape of its stories.
book.book317.title: The Raven
book.book317.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book.book317.description: Midnight, a grieving man, and a bird that will not leave the doorway and has only one word to offer. Heavy internal rhyme drags the dread along with it, and the ending refuses every scrap of comfort.
book.book318.title: The Sea of Monsters; (Percy Jackson #2)
book.book318.author: Rick Riordan
book.book318.description: Camp Half-Blood's magical border is failing and the only cure is a Golden Fleece somewhere in the Sea of Monsters, which modern charts call the Bermuda Triangle. Percy's second outing, with a crew he did not pick.
book.book320.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
book.book320.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
book.book320.description: A reclusive film legend agrees at last to tell the truth about her seven marriages, and picks an unknown magazine writer to hear it. Old Hollywood glamour over a love story the studios would never have allowed.
book.book321.title: The Seven Lamps of Architecture
book.book321.author: John Ruskin
book.book321.description: Seven principles a building ought to obey, from sacrifice to memory, argued with Victorian certainty and a passion for Gothic stone. Dense, sermon-like prose for readers who want architecture as a moral question.
book.book322.title: The Shining
book.book322.author: Stephen King
book.book322.description: Winter caretaker at a grand empty hotel sounds like the fresh start a drinking writer needs, and his small son already knows better. Months of snow, a boiler wanting attention, and a building with an appetite for families.
book.book323.title: The Silence of the Lambs
book.book323.author: Thomas Harris
book.book323.description: A trainee agent is sent to trade scraps of her own history with a caged psychiatrist, because he may know who is skinning women in the Midwest. Two interrogations running at once, only one of them official. Still the benchmark.
book.book324.title: The Silmarillion
book.book324.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book.book324.description: Before any hobbits, there was a song that made the world, three jewels holding the last of its light, and an oath sworn by their maker that doomed everyone who kept it. Scripture-dry, mythic, relentlessly tragic.
book.book325.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
book.book325.author: Unknown & Simon Armitage
book.book325.description: Into a Christmas feast rides a green giant who offers his neck to any taker, then names the price: find him in a year and kneel for the return blow. Alliterative verse, bristling with hunts and temptation.
book.book326.title: Siren Queen
book.book326.author: Nghi Vo
book.book326.description: In a Hollywood where studio contracts are signed in blood and fire, a Chinese American girl refuses to play the maid and takes the monster roles instead. Glamour, hunger and real magic, told without apology.
book.book327.title: The Song of Achilles
book.book327.author: Madeline Miller
book.book327.description: Exiled prince Patroclus is taken in by the golden son of a sea goddess, and boyhood friendship walks them both to the beach at Troy. Miller retells the Iliad as a love story, knowing exactly how myth ends.
book.book328.title: Sorcery and Small Magics; The Wildersongs Trilogy #1
book.book328.author: Maiga Doocy
book.book328.description: Leovander writes charming little spells and no serious ones. Grimm can cast anything and despises him. One botched curse later they are stuck together on the road to the Unquiet Wood. Enemies to something else, sweetly done.
book.book329.title: Soul Music; Discworld #16, Death #3
book.book329.author: Terry Pratchett
book.book329.description: Music With Rocks In arrives in Ankh-Morpork out of a shop that was not there yesterday, and it will not stop. Death has wandered off to forget something, leaving his granddaughter holding the scythe. Daft, and oddly moving.
book.book330.title: The Soul of Man Under Socialism
book.book330.author: Oscar Wilde
book.book330.description: Socialism defended not for the sake of the state but so that people might finally become individuals and make art. A short, contrary, gleefully argumentative essay that treats charity itself as part of the problem.
book.book331.title: The Spear Cuts Through Water
book.book331.author: Simon Jimenez
book.book331.description: Two young men carry a dying god across a country in five nights, hunted by the emperor's sons. Jimenez stages the whole thing as a performance watched from a dream: gorgeous, brutal, and well over five hundred pages.
book.book332.title: The Stand
book.book332.author: Stephen King
book.book332.description: Ninety-nine percent of America dies of the flu inside a fortnight. The few left start dreaming of an old woman in Nebraska or a smiling man out west, and walk toward one of them. Over a thousand pages, all of them earned.
book.book333.title: The Story Girl; Book 1
book.book333.author: L.M. Montgomery
book.book333.description: One summer, cousins run loose in a Prince Edward Island orchard, where a girl tells a story so well that the others forget their chores and their suppers. Episodes, jokes, one glorious doomsday panic.
book.book335.title: The Tell-Tale Heart
book.book335.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book.book335.description: The narrator would like it understood that he is not mad, merely sharp of hearing, and that the old man's clouded eye left him no choice at all. Thirty pages of murder told by the least trustworthy voice in the language.
book.book336.title: The Tempest
book.book336.author: William Shakespeare
book.book336.description: Marooned on an island with his books, his daughter and two unwilling servants, a deposed duke raises a storm to wash his enemies ashore. Late Shakespeare, thick with magic, music and bargained forgiveness.
book.book337.title: The Templars; The Rise and Spectacular Fall of God's Holy Warriors
book.book337.author: Dan Jones
book.book337.description: Bankers in armour, sworn to poverty, grown rich enough to frighten kings and then broken by one. Narrative history of the warrior order, well sourced and fast moving, for readers who like medieval politics sharp.
book.book338.title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
book.book338.author: Anne Brontë
book.book338.description: Nobody knows the widow who moves into the half-ruined hall with her small son, paints for money and refuses to explain herself, until her diary does. Unsparing about a drunk husband, and meant to shock.
book.book339.title: The Traitor Baru Cormorant; (The Masquerade #1)
book.book339.author: Seth Dickinson
book.book339.description: Her island is annexed by an empire that conquers with schools, sanitation and eugenics, so Baru learns its accounting and climbs. Rebellion fought with ledgers and currency crashes, at a cost the arithmetic never covers.
book.book340.title: A Tramp Abroad
book.book340.author: Mark Twain
book.book340.description: Walking tour of Germany and the Alps, conducted mostly by raft, carriage and any transport that is not walking. Dated in places, still very funny about mountains, opera and the German language.
book.book341.title: The Travels of Marco Polo
book.book341.author: Marco Polo
book.book341.description: Dictated in a Genoese prison: caravans to the court of the Great Khan, cities of a size Europe refused to believe, and the occasional dragon. Wildly unreliable, and wildly worth the trip.
book.book342.title: Wars of The Roses; The Fall of the Plantagenets and the Rise of the Tudors
book.book342.author: Dan Jones
book.book342.description: Cousins with armies, a crown that kept changing heads, and a dynastic war that ended with a new family on the throne. Popular narrative history, briskly told, strong on battles and stronger on the people.
book.book343.title: War and Peace
book.book343.author: Leo Tolstoy
book.book343.description: Five families, twenty years, Napoleon coming and going, and Pierre wandering a battlefield trying to work out what he is looking at. Ballrooms, retreats and long essays on history; give it a whole winter.
book.book344.title: The War of the Worlds
book.book344.author: H. G. Wells
book.book344.description: Something unscrews the lid of a cylinder on Horsell Common, and within days tripods are walking over Surrey burning everything ahead of them. Told by an ordinary man trying to get home. The blueprint for every invasion since.
book.book345.title: The Well at the World's End
book.book345.author: William Morris
book.book345.description: Ralph, youngest son of a very small king, rides out after a well at the edge of the world whose water grants long life and luck. Written in deliberate medieval English, and one of the roots the whole genre grew from.
book.book346.title: The Wilder Shores of Love
book.book346.author: Lesley Blanch
book.book346.description: Four nineteenth-century women who went east and declined to come home to the drawing room, told as romantic biography with the scholarship worn lightly. Sumptuous, dated in its attitudes, and a very good read.
book.book347.title: Will You Love Me?; The story of my adopted daughter Lucy
book.book347.author: Cathy Glass
book.book347.description: A foster carer's account of one girl who arrives angry, hungry and certain she will be moved on again. Plain, quick, upsetting in places, and it does end somewhere hopeful. Written from inside the care system.
book.book348.title: The Willows
book.book348.author: Algernon Blackwood
book.book348.description: Two men canoe down the Danube and camp on a sandbank among endless willows, where the sand shifts, the bushes move and something enormous takes an interest. Barely a hundred pages, and among the finest horror in English.
book.book349.title: The Woman in White
book.book349.author: Wilkie Collins
book.book349.description: Midnight on a lonely road, one stranger dressed in white, and an inheritance worth ruining a woman for. Sworn testimonies fit slowly together: Victorian sensation at full pitch, cruel in places and tender in others.
book.book350.title: Women Travel Solo; 30 Inspiring Stories of Adventure, Curiosity and the Power of Self-Discovery
book.book350.author: Various Authors
book.book350.description: Thirty women, thirty solo departures, and thirty accounts of what curiosity does to a person who goes alone. Warm, brisk company for anyone still talking themselves into booking the ticket.
book.book351.title: Women, Race and Class
book.book351.author: Angela Y. Davis
book.book351.description: Abolition, suffrage, housework and wages, read together to show where the women's movement failed Black women and working women. A sharp, foundational history of feminism's blind spots, argued from the record.
book.book352.title: Working Songs of Bookstonbury
book.book352.author: Edwin Kimble
book.book352.description: A collection of traditional shanties and sea songs by sailors and dockworkers around Bookstonbury harbour. Contains some old classics, as well as lesser-known local songs like The Net-Eating Shark and Even The Seagulls Like A Good Book .
book.book353.title: The Yellow Fairy Book
book.book353.author: L. B. Alleyne & A. Lang
book.book353.description: Dozens of tales gathered from Norse, Russian, Hungarian and Native American sources, with emperors, witches and talking birds among them. One volume of the coloured series that shaped the fairy-tale shelf.
book.book354.title: Yellowface
book.book354.author: R.F. Kuang
book.book354.description: Publishing is a small world, and a stolen manuscript is a very loud secret. Sharp, gossipy, horribly funny satire that keeps twisting the knife about who gets to tell whose story, and who gets paid for it.
book.book355.title: Theodora Hendrix and the Curious Case of the Cursed Beetle
book.book355.author: Jordan Kopy
book.book355.description: Monsters, curses and a beetle that plainly should have been left alone. Recent middle-grade spookiness, long enough to last a week of bedtimes, and creepy in the cheerful way rather than the sleepless way.
book.book356.title: There's A Ghost In This House
book.book356.author: Oliver Jeffers
book.book356.description: A girl gives you a tour of her house, certain that a ghost lives somewhere in it, while tracing-paper overlays keep showing exactly what she misses. A picture book that turns page-turning into the joke.
book.book357.title: They Both Die at the End
book.book357.author: Adam Silvera
book.book357.description: Death-Cast rings before dawn to say today is your last, so Mateo and Rufus find each other on an app for final friends and spend the day living properly. The title warned you. It hurts anyway.
book.book358.title: The Third Gilmore Girl; A Memoir
book.book358.author: Kelly Bishop
book.book358.description: Broadway first, dancing eight shows a week, then decades of television and one famously formidable grandmother. A performer's memoir, brisk and candid about work, marriages and the business of being cast.
book.book359.title: This Book Will Bury Me
book.book359.author: Ashley Winstead
book.book359.description: Long, dark and deliberately nasty contemporary crime, heavy on dread and worse, for readers who want a mystery that keeps twisting and never once flinches at the ugly parts.
book.book360.title: Titus Andronicus
book.book360.author: William Shakespeare
book.book360.description: Rome's victorious general sacrifices a Gothic queen's son, and she spends the rest of the play answering him. Shakespeare's earliest tragedy is a revenge machine, notorious for staging its cruelty rather than reporting it.
book.book361.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
book.book361.author: Harper Lee
book.book361.description: Scout is six, her town is small and Alabama hot, and her father takes the case nobody wants him to take. Half a funny childhood summer, half a courtroom that ends the way the grown-ups always knew it would.
book.book362.title: To the Lighthouse
book.book362.author: Virginia Woolf
book.book362.description: Skye, a summer house, a promised trip across the bay, and a dinner party held together by sheer will. Almost nothing happens out loud, the deaths arrive in brackets, and the last pages repay the effort.
book.book363.title: A Tomb With a View; The Stories and Glories of Graveyards
book.book363.author: Peter Ross
book.book363.description: Graveyards as places where the living gather: keepers, historians, mourners and the odd celebrity resident. Reported essays wandering the burial grounds of Britain and Ireland, funnier and kinder than expected.
book.book364.title: Treasure Island
book.book364.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
book.book364.description: Jim finds a map at the inn where his father is dying, and the ship hired to chase it is crewed by exactly the wrong men. A one-legged sea cook, an island stockade, and not a wasted chapter anywhere.
book.book365.title: Tree Houses: Baumhäuser - Maisons Dans les Arbres
book.book365.author: Philip Jodidio
book.book365.description: Houses up in the branches, from plank-and-rope forts grown up to engineered retreats with glass and cantilevers. A big photographic survey of building in trees, better for browsing than for following literally.
book.book366.title: True Beauty; Volume 1
book.book366.author: Yaongyi
book.book366.description: Jugyeong learns makeup from internet tutorials and walks into school as the pretty girl, terrified of being seen without it. First volume of the Korean webtoon, a school romance with real bite under the gloss.
book.book367.title: True Crime Story
book.book367.author: Joseph Knox
book.book367.description: One student vanishes from a Manchester tower block, and the case resurfaces years later as interviews, emails and flat contradictions. Assembled like a real documentary, which is what makes it unsettling.
book.book368.title: True Grit
book.book368.author: Charles Portis
book.book368.description: Mattie Ross is fourteen, her father is dead, and the one-eyed marshal she hires would rather drink than ride. Her account of the manhunt is bone dry and funnier than the body count suggests.
book.book369.title: The Truth; Discworld #25, Industrial Revolution #2
book.book369.author: Terry Pratchett
book.book369.description: Movable type reaches Ankh-Morpork and William de Worde, who only wanted to write a newsletter, finds himself running a newspaper while somebody frames the Patrician. Dwarfs, a vampire on the pictures, and a dog with a scoop.
book.book370.title: Tuesdays with Morrie
book.book370.author: Mitch Alborn
book.book370.description: Every Tuesday a former student sits with the old professor who is dying of ALS and still teaching. Conversations about work, family and regret, set down as a last course with no exam at the end.
book.book371.title: The Turn of the Screw
book.book371.author: Henry James
book.book371.description: A young governess takes charge of two unnervingly polite children in a country house and starts seeing figures nobody else will admit to. Barely 120 pages, and every one can be read two ways.
book.book372.title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
book.book372.author: Jules Verne
book.book372.description: Harpooned into the custody of Captain Nemo, a naturalist tours the sea floor aboard a submarine that answers to no flag. Expect squid, coral forests, and page after page of loving specimen lists.
book.book373.title: Twisted Love
book.book373.author: Ana Huang
book.book373.description: Ava's brother leaves his cold, ruthless best friend in charge of looking after her, which is how a man who claims to feel nothing ends up wrecked. Steamy contemporary romance, first of a series, and firmly for adults.
book.book374.title: The Unmaking of June Farrow
book.book374.author: Adrienne Young
book.book374.description: June inherits the family flower farm and the family affliction: voices, a door nobody else can see, and a mother who disappeared without explanation. Half missing-person case, half love story across time.
book.book375.title: Unmasking Autism
book.book375.author: Devon Price
book.book375.description: Masking to pass as neurotypical costs more than it earns: a social psychologist's case for dropping the performance, built from interviews with late-diagnosed autistic and queer adults, plus exercises for finding your own footing.
book.book376.title: The Unusual Suspects; The Sisters Grimm #2
book.book376.author: Michael Buckley, Peter Ferguson (Illustrator)
book.book376.description: Two sisters go undercover at a school where the teachers stepped straight out of old fairy tales, one of them now extremely dead and something enormous stirring underground. Funny, fast and crawling with monsters.
book.book377.title: Unwitting Wisdom; An Anthology of Aesop's Animal Fables
book.book377.author: Helen Ward
book.book377.description: Foxes flatter, tortoises plod, and each one hands you a moral on the way out. Aesop's animals retold in a handful of short fables, painted in the sort of detail that rewards holding the page close.
book.book378.title: Upgrading and Repairing PCs
book.book378.author: Scott Mueller
book.book378.description: Nearly thirteen hundred pages on motherboards, drive interfaces and power supplies, revised edition after edition for anyone who opens the case themselves. Dry as a service manual, and indexed like one too.
book.book379.title: Valperga
book.book379.author: Mary Shelley
book.book379.description: A boyhood friend grows into a warlord, and the woman who loves him will not hand over her free city to buy his affection. Medieval Italy, prophecy and politics, with no comfortable ending waiting.
book.book380.title: Vera Wong's Unsolicited Advice for Murderers; Vera Wong #1
book.book380.author: Jesse Q. Sutanto
book.book380.description: Vera runs a tea shop nobody visits, finds a dead man on the floor, quietly pockets the evidence and invites the suspects round for oolong. Nosy, bossy and completely delightful cozy sleuthing.
book.book381.title: Villainous Victorians; Horrible Histories
book.book381.author: Terry Deary
book.book381.description: Victorian Britain served up with the gruesome bits left in: chimney sweeps, grim punishments, cheerful cartoons and jokes at every turn. History for kids who prefer their facts a bit revolting, from a long-running series.
book.book382.title: Villette
book.book382.author: Charlotte Brontë
book.book382.description: Lucy Snowe crosses the Channel with no money and no plan, and takes a teaching post in a foreign city where nobody knows her. Bronte at her coldest and strangest, five hundred pages of watchful loneliness.
book.book383.title: Violets Are Blue
book.book383.author: James Patterson
book.book383.description: Bodies drained of blood in the Pacific Northwest, killers who believe they are vampires, and a Washington detective who cannot shake the taunts of an old enemy. Grim, quick, built for one sitting.
book.book384.title: Watchmen; (Issue #12)
book.book384.author: Alan Moore
book.book384.description: Somebody throws a costumed vigilante out of a high window, and a paranoid man in an inkblot mask starts asking why. Superheroes as a Cold War liability, drawn nine panels to the page, where the doomsday clock is not a metaphor.
book.book385.title: Watership Down
book.book385.author: Richard Adams
book.book385.description: Their warren is doomed, so a handful of rabbits walk out on the strength of one runt's vision and go looking for high ground. Own language, own myths, and a death toll that startles readers expecting cuddly.
book.book386.title: Where the Wild Things Are
book.book386.author: Maurice Sendak
book.book386.description: Sent to bed without supper in his wolf suit, a boy sails off to be crowned king of some very toothy monsters. Ten sentences, enormous pictures, and a last page about supper still being warm.
book.book387.title: White Teeth
book.book387.author: Zadie Smith
book.book387.description: Two old army friends, one English and one Bengali, raise their children in north London and make a hash of it in three directions at once. Smith's big comic novel of immigration, faith and inherited arguments.
book.book388.title: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?
book.book388.author: Edward Albee
book.book388.description: Late-night drinking, two faculty couples, and party games with names like Get the Guest. Three acts made of dialogue that lands like a knife fight, and the laughs keep arriving sideways.
book.book389.title: Wuthering Heights
book.book389.author: Emily Brontë
book.book389.description: A farmer brings home a foundling boy, and forty years later the moors are still paying for it. Bronte's novel of obsession dressed as love, narrated by a housekeeper who saw everything and forgave almost none of it.
book.book390.title: You've Reached Sam
book.book390.author: Dustin Thao
book.book390.description: Sam is dead, but when Julie calls his number he picks up. A novel about a girl granted a few more conversations than she is owed, and the harder question of when to stop dialling.
book.book391.title: By Train Through Spain
book.book391.author: Amerigo Marchesi
book.book391.description: Join this charming and colourful journey across Spain with Amerigo Marchesi as they hop on trains, capture stunning vistas and uncover fascinating hidden gems.
book.book392.title: Discovering the Greater Bookston Region
book.book392.author: Peter Spinner
book.book392.description: Join Peter Spinner as he looks for the well-kept hidden gems of the enchanting Greater Bookston Region. High-quality restaurants, cosy stays, endearing shops, and local events await!
book.book393.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 2
book.book393.author: Ash Axbridge
book.book393.description: Get ready for a mind-blowing journey through the wondrous world of knowledge! Volume 2 of Encyclopaedia Bookstonia: from D as in Detective Novels to J as in Japanese Manga.
book.book394.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 3
book.book394.author: Ash Axbridge
book.book394.description: Discover a world of knowledge and adventure in this thrilling third volume of Encyclopaedia Bookstonia. From K as in Knitting Instructions to O as in Omegaverse.
book.book395.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 4
book.book395.author: Ash Axbridge
book.book395.description: Another epic volume filled with knowledge and wonder! What else does this encyclopaedia series have in store? I'll tell you: Entries from P as in Philosophy to T as in True Crime.
book.book396.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 5
book.book396.author: Ash Axbridge
book.book396.description: Vol. 5 of this encyclopaedia concludes our journey of learning, with the entries we've all been waiting for: U as in Unfinished Manuscripts to Y as in Yuri. (They forgot to print Z).
book.book397.title: The Encyclopedia of the Weird and Wonderful; Curious and Incredible Facts that Will Blow Your Mind
book.book397.author: Milo Rossi
book.book397.description: Short entries on the odd corners of nature, the earth and the past, arranged to be dipped into rather than read straight through. Curious facts for browsers of any age who enjoy being surprised mid-page.
book.book398.title: Finding Optimism; The Future Is Good
book.book398.author: Liliane Renaud
book.book398.description: Liliane Renaud believes that, despite everything, the future must be bright. This solarpunk-inspired work is packed with thoughtful poems and practical insights to guide you through life's most difficult challenges.
book.book399.title: Herbcraft; The Power of Natural Healing and Hexing
book.book399.author: Star Ravenhunt
book.book399.description: Get ready to brew up some magic as Star Ravenhunt shares the secrets of herbcraft, from natural healing potions to delicious recipes to mischievous hexes.
book.book400.title: Here Be Dragons; (Welsh Princes #1)
book.book400.author: Sharon Kay Penman
book.book400.description: Llewelyn rules Wales by war and marriage; his wife is an English king's illegitimate daughter, loyal to both men and forced to choose. Eight hundred pages of thirteenth-century politics, book one of three.
book.book401.title: Historical Niche
book.book401.author: Terry Czernik
book.book401.description: This in-depth exploration of the Danelaw by a scholar of history promises sophisticated insights for anyone with an interest in 886–1066 AD in Northern England.
book.book402.title: HTML 1998; An Introdcution
book.book402.author: Hello Worldly
book.book402.description: Get ready to enter the digital world with this 90s guide to HTML (specifically 3.2), the language that powers the internet. Let's say "Hello, World!"
book.book403.title: In Search Of:; The Most Beautiful Islands In the World
book.book403.author: Je Hyun
book.book403.description: The newest entry in our In Search Of series: A marvellous view across stunning islands, where paradise awaits at every turn, even if you're on a budget.
book.book404.title: Just A Story: Why We Still Tell Fairytales
book.book404.author: Isabel Galvan
book.book404.description: Once upon a time... there was the captivating world of fairytales. Discover why these timeless tales continue to enchant and intrigue us in this cultural and anthropological study.
book.book405.title: Kitchen Rules For Your Family and You
book.book405.author: Mbwana Jones
book.book405.description: Spice up your family's kitchen adventures with this delightful guide. From cooking tips to family bonding, discover the recipe for a happy home!
book.book406.title: Know My Name
book.book406.author: Chanel Miller
book.book406.description: Reclaiming a name after being known only as a victim in a court transcript: a memoir of assault, a trial that failed her, and the slow work of becoming whole again. Devastating, and written with real grace.
book.book407.title: Living In Alaska
book.book407.author: Sioned Jones
book.book407.description: This chilling page-turner, based on Jones' true story, will take you on a wild journey through the frozen wilderness of Alaska, filled with heartbreak, resilience, and unexpected turns.
book.book408.title: The Long Unwinding Road; A Journey through the Heart of Wales
book.book408.author: Marc P Jones
book.book408.description: Come with Marc P Jones as he takes you through the beautiful green hills and valleys of Wales. Discover Wales' deep majesty and ancient history, with local voices at the fore.
book.book409.title: Medieval Carpentry
book.book409.author: Obu Henderson
book.book409.description: Woodworking tips and tricks from the days of knights and castles. Unearth ancient techniques and bring medieval craftsmanship back to life!
book.book410.title: Mesopotamian Buildings
book.book410.author: Ahmed Mansour
book.book410.description: Discover the awe-inspiring marvels crafted by ancient hands in this fascinating delve into Mesopotamian architecture. Join us on a journey through time!
book.book411.title: Physics 1908
book.book411.author: Kendra Conelli
book.book411.description: Discover the captivating world of physics through a historical journey that will tickle your brain and transport you to 1908.
book.book412.title: Round Luxembourg with Brooke
book.book412.author: Brooke Dixon
book.book412.description: Join rising Instagram star BrookeTravels on an adventure through Luxembourg as she explores, shares delicious recipes, and provides a refreshing take on travel and lifestyle.
book.book413.title: Round the World in Eighty Dishes
book.book413.author: Lesley Blanch
book.book413.description: Travel by dinner plate: a slim cookbook that tours the world one recipe at a time, chatty about each country's table. Charming, and dated enough that half the pleasure is the period itself.
book.book414.title: St. Bookston: The Myth, the Legend, the Truth
book.book414.author: H. A. Pennington
book.book414.description: The most brilliant writer and philosopher of his time. But who was he really? And why do we know so little about his life? Finally uncover the truth in this groundbreaking investigative biography.
book.book415.title: The Debvoir Family; A Success Story
book.book415.author: Kennedy Naybon
book.book415.description: Follow the triumphs and trials of a remarkable family, as the Debvoir clan shapes and is challenged by the very history of Bookstonbury.
book.book416.title: Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen
book.book416.author: Olympe de Gouges
book.book416.description: Seventeen articles, rewritten line by line from the French revolution's own declaration with the women put back into it. Thirty pages of argument that helped send its author to the guillotine.
book.book417.title: Top 50 Camper Van Destinations
book.book417.author: Tamir Ghasti
book.book417.description: From winding coastal roads to serene mountain retreats, this comprehensive camping guide unveils a collection of breathtaking landscapes and hidden gems.
book.book418.title: Topdog/Underdog
book.book418.author: Suzan-Lori Parks
book.book418.description: Two brothers, one rented room, a deck of cards and a hustle neither can quite leave alone. A short, savage, wickedly funny play about money, blood ties and the con that never stops paying.
book.book419.title: Traditional Building Techniques
book.book419.author: Lohar Bishmal
book.book419.description: Have you ever looked at an old city's houses, castles and bridges and asked yourself: "How did they build that"? This book illustrates the greatest building techniques of all time and what we can learn from them today.
book.book420.title: A Clash of Kings
book.book420.author: George R. R. Martin
book.book420.description: A comet the colour of blood hangs over Westeros while five men claim one throne and none will back down. The second volume, where the war stops being theoretical and magic starts creeping back. Seven hundred pages, no mercy.
book.book421.title: The Code Book; The Science of Secrecy from Ancient Egypt to Quantum Cryptography
book.book421.author: Simon Singh
book.book421.description: Ciphers, and the people who broke them: a queen undone by a cracked code, Enigma unpicked at Bletchley, lost scripts deciphered at last. Popular history of secret writing that teaches the maths painlessly.
book.book422.title: A Court of Mist and Fury
book.book422.author: Sarah J. Maas
book.book422.description: Book two turns the Courts inside out. A bargain drags Feyre to the Night Court one week a month, where the male everyone fears turns out to be playing a far longer game. Faerie politics, slow-burn romance, and a war coming.
book.book423.title: The Cream Tea Killer
book.book423.author: Judy Leigh
book.book423.description: Cozy crime with a tearoom appetite: light, brisk, gently nosy, and part of a series that treats a killing as something to be sorted out over a warm scone and a very strong pot of tea.
book.book424.title: A Feast for Crows
book.book424.author: George R. R. Martin
book.book424.description: The war is over, in the sense that the armies are gone and the wreckage is not. Volume four moves to a kingsmoot, to Dorne, to a capital run by someone with no gift for it, while a tall knight searches the ruined roads.
book.book425.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
book.book425.author: William Shakespeare
book.book425.description: Four lovers run into a wood ruled by quarrelling fairies, a meddling sprite with the wrong flower, and a troupe of amateurs rehearsing the worst play ever staged. Shakespeare's comedy at its silliest and best.
book.book426.title: Walden
book.book426.author: Henry David Thoreau
book.book426.description: Two years in a self-built cabin beside a pond, with the bean field accounted for down to the cent. Half nature notebook, half lecture on how little a person needs, and not at all shy about the lecturing.
book.book427.title: A Walk in the Woods
book.book427.author: Bill Bryson
book.book427.description: Two unfit friends set out to walk two thousand miles of the Appalachian Trail with the wrong gear and no plan at all. Bears, snack food, forest history, and a great deal of complaining.
book.book428.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
book.book428.author: Lewis Carroll
book.book428.description: Follow a waistcoated rabbit down a hole and the rules stop applying: a caterpillar on a hookah, a tea party with no end, a queen who sentences first. Nonsense logic, verse and riddles, none of it dated.
book.book429.title: All My Sons
book.book429.author: Arthur Miller
book.book429.description: A backyard in a comfortable American town, a son still missing from the war, and a business decision the family has agreed never to mention. Miller's short tragedy tightens over one day until the neighbours hear it.
book.book430.title: All Out; The No-Longer-Secret Stories of Queer Teens throughout the Ages
book.book430.author: Various Authors
book.book430.description: Queer teenagers turn up where history usually erases them: an outlaw band in Sherwood, a Georgian country house, a small-town roller rink. Short stories spanning centuries, every one of them about a first love.
book.book431.title: All She Was Worth
book.book431.author: Miyuki Miyabe
book.book431.description: Sick leave gives a Tokyo detective time to look for a relative's missing fiancee, and the trail runs through debt, borrowed names and lives bought secondhand. Japanese crime writing at its quietest and most furious.
book.book432.title: All Systems Red; The Murderbot Diaries #1
book.book432.author: Martha Wells
book.book432.description: Murderbot hacked its own governor module and now mostly wants to be left alone with several thousand hours of soap opera. Instead it has to keep a survey team alive on a hostile world. Short, deadpan, quietly anxious.
book.book433.title: All Your Twisted Secrets
book.book433.author: Diana Urban
book.book433.description: Six teenagers, one locked room, a syringe on the table and a note demanding that one of them die before the timer runs down. Sharp teen suspense that keeps cutting back to how they all got invited.
book.book434.title: All's Well That Ends Well
book.book434.author: William Shakespeare
book.book434.description: Helena cures a king and asks for a husband as payment. The husband runs off to a war rather than have her. Shakespeare's most awkward comedy, in which the woman does all the scheming and the title makes a promise.
book.book435.title: Allegiant; Divergent #3
book.book435.author: Veronica Roth
book.book435.description: Tris finally gets past the fence and finds the people who have been watching Chicago all along. The third Divergent book splits its narration in two and ends the series somewhere readers still argue about.
book.book436.title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
book.book436.author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
book.book436.description: In a Tokyo basement cafe one seat sends you back in time, and the rules are strict: nothing you do will change the present, and you must finish before the coffee cools. Four quiet stories about the thing left unsaid.
book.book437.title: Belinda
book.book437.author: Maria Edgeworth
book.book437.description: Belinda is brought to London to be marketed for marriage and finds her glamorous chaperone hiding a ruined life under the rouge. Long, moralising, and sharper about reputation than the manners suggest.
book.book438.title: Beowulf
book.book438.author: Unknown, transl. by S. Heaney
book.book438.description: A hero sails to a hall where a monster comes nightly, and fifty years on he meets a dragon. Heaney's translation gives the great Old English epic a plain, hammering music that makes the oldest lines sound alive.
book.book439.title: The Best Short Stories of O. Henry
book.book439.author: O. Henry, B. Cerf & V.H. Cartmell
book.book439.description: New York shop girls, safecrackers, cowboys and con men, every story turning on its final sentence. O. Henry's twist endings collected whole: sentimental, sharp, and dated in ways that show their age.
book.book440.title: Blood of Elves; (The Witcher)
book.book440.author: Andrzej Sapkowski
book.book440.description: The first full novel of the Witcher saga. A child of prophecy is hidden at the witchers' mountain keep and trained to survive, while every power on the Continent works out what she is worth. Politics sharpen, monsters recede.
book.book441.title: Blood, Sweat, and Pixels
book.book441.author: Jason Schreier
book.book441.description: Ten video games, ten different ways a project nearly collapsed before shipping. Reported from inside the studios, full of crunch, rewrites and last-minute rescues, and surprisingly breezy for a book about misery.
book.book442.title: The Blue Castle
book.book442.author: L.M. Montgomery
book.book442.description: Valancy is twenty-nine, unmarried and bullied by her relatives until a doctor's letter convinces her that she has one year left. So she says what she thinks and moves to the woods. Montgomery for grown-ups.
book.book443.title: Blue Highways; The Travel Trilogy #1
book.book443.author: William Least Heat-Moon
book.book443.description: Back roads once printed in blue on old maps carry a man in a van around the whole edge of America, stopping wherever someone will talk. First of a trilogy, and still the measure for slow travel done properly.
book.book444.title: Blue Sisters
book.book444.author: Coco Mellors
book.book444.description: Three sisters, a lawyer, a boxer and a model, return to the New York apartment they grew up in a year after the fourth one died. Addiction, grief and old scores, handled without flinching or tidying up.
book.book445.title: Carrie
book.book445.author: Stephen King
book.book445.description: Inquest transcripts, letters and survivor statements circle one small-town catastrophe and the bullied girl at its centre, whose strange power nobody believed in until it was far too late.
book.book446.title: Case Closed; One and the Same? (Vol. 3)
book.book446.author: Gosho Aoyama
book.book446.description: A teenage detective trapped in a child's body keeps cracking cases nobody will let him take credit for. Compact, fairly clued puzzles in comic form, this volume built around a problem of look-alikes.
book.book447.title: Catching Fire
book.book447.author: Suzanne Collins
book.book447.description: The districts are simmering, the Capitol needs a distraction, and the seventy-fifth Games arrive with a rule nobody survives twice. Volume two, where a stunt becomes a symbol and a symbol becomes a war.
book.book448.title: Cats in Space... and Other Places
book.book448.author: Various Authors
book.book448.description: An anthology of science fiction and fantasy stories with one thing in common: a cat somewhere in them, usually the one with a plan. Space travel, stranger places, and four hundred pages of cheerfully niche fun.
book.book449.title: Caturday in Bookstonbury; Volume 2
book.book449.author: Luna Knight
book.book449.description: In this visual photographic history of Bookstonbury, Luna Knight documents the local feline population. From majestic longhairs to playful shorthairs and everything in between, take a gander and learn more about these adorable floofs.
book.book450.title: The Caucasian Chalk Circle
book.book450.author: Bertolt Brecht
book.book450.description: A servant girl carries an abandoned baby across the mountains, and years later a drunkard of a judge must decide whose child it is. Brecht's parable play about who has earned the things they claim to own.
book.book451.title: Cemetery Boys
book.book451.author: Aiden Thomas
book.book451.description: Yadriel wants his family to accept him as a brujo, so he summons a spirit to prove it and gets the wrong ghost entirely: a loud, charming boy who refuses to move on until his own death is explained.
book.book452.title: Chain-Gang All-Stars
book.book452.author: Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah
book.book452.description: Prisoners fight to the death on live television for a shot at freedom, and the ratings are excellent. Thurwar is a few matches from release. Savage satire of American incarceration, footnoted with the real thing.
book.book453.title: The Chalk Man
book.book453.author: C.J. Tudor
book.book453.description: Chalk figures on the pavement were a private code between friends one long summer, until one of them pointed the way to a body in the woods. Decades later the drawings start again. Nasty, nostalgic, dread-soaked.
book.book455.title: Crime and Punishment
book.book455.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
book.book455.description: A broke student murders a pawnbroker to test a theory about great men, then spends hundreds of pages being taken apart by his own conscience and a policeman who never quite accuses him. Feverish, airless.
book.book456.title: Critical Hits; Writers on Gaming and the Alternate Worlds We Inhabit
book.book456.author: Various Authors
book.book456.description: Novelists and poets writing about the games that got under their skin, from open-world wandering to character creators and the pull of an unfinished save. A slim essay collection, personal rather than technical.
book.book457.title: The CRPG Book; Guide to Computer Role-Playing Games
book.book457.author: Collection
book.book457.description: Hundreds of computer role-playing games reviewed by the fans who played them, decade by decade, with screenshots and strong opinions. Huge, browsable, and the closest thing the genre has to a family album.
book.book458.title: Don Quixote
book.book458.author: Miguel de Cervantes
book.book458.description: An old man reads too much chivalric romance, names a bony horse Rocinante and rides out to right wrongs only he can see. A thousand pages of slapstick that turns sad once you notice who is laughing.
book.book459.title: Don't Let the Forest In
book.book459.author: C.G. Drews
book.book459.description: Andrew writes monsters, Thomas draws them, and behind their boarding school the drawings wait in the trees with too many teeth. Queer teen horror where the bleeding hands and the aching crush arrive together.
book.book460.title: Dune
book.book460.author: Frank Herbert
book.book460.description: One desert planet yields the spice that makes interstellar travel possible, so whoever holds Arrakis holds everything. A ducal heir loses his house and finds a prophecy waiting in the sand. Ecology, religion and empire, welded.
book.book461.title: East of Eden
book.book461.author: John Steinbeck
book.book461.description: Two generations of Trasks farm the Salinas Valley and keep replaying Cain and Abel, with a mother who walked out of the house and into a brothel. Long, biblical, and greenest when it stops to look at the land.
book.book462.title: Edinburgh; Picturesque Notes
book.book462.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
book.book462.description: Wind, wet stone and a city stacked along a ridge, walked through in short essays by a native who loves it and refuses to pretend the weather is bearable. Closes, kirkyards and gossip, under 130 pages.
book.book463.title: The Eleventh Hour; A Curious Mystery
book.book463.author: Graeme Base
book.book463.description: An elephant throws an eleventh birthday party for eleven animal guests, and someone eats the feast before the clock strikes. Rhyming verse over densely coded pictures, with the solution sealed at the back.
book.book464.title: Elsewhere; One Woman, One Rucksack, One Lifetime of Travel
book.book464.author: Rosita Boland
book.book464.description: One rucksack, decades of departures, and a reporter's eye for the strangers who turn up when you travel alone. A memoir assembled from single journeys, each carrying its own weight of wonder and loss.
book.book465.title: Fire & Blood
book.book465.author: George R. R. Martin
book.book465.description: Not a novel but a maester's chronicle: generations of Targaryen rule, dragon by dragon, from the Conquest to the civil war that burned the dynasty's power out. Dry, gossipy, and full of sources that contradict each other.
book.book466.title: Frank Lloyd Wright
book.book466.author: Frank Lloyd Wright
book.book466.description: Plates, plans and a short critical text on one of architecture's most argued-over careers. Slim, academic in tone, and aimed at readers who already know the buildings and now want the drawings.
book.book467.title: Frankenstein
book.book467.author: Mary Shelley
book.book467.description: Victor Frankenstein assembles a living man and runs from him the moment those eyes open. The creature teaches itself to read, to speak, and to ask why it was made. The first science fiction novel, and still the most pitiless.
book.book468.title: Ghost Stories; From the Grave
book.book468.author: Collection
book.book468.description: Short, shivery tales gathered for one dark evening: a slim collection that prefers atmosphere and unanswered questions to tidy explanations, and can be finished before the candle burns down.
book.book469.title: Great Big Beautiful Life
book.book469.author: Emily Henry
book.book469.description: Two rival writers land on a Georgia island, each given one month to win over the reclusive heiress whose scandalous family they want to write. Sunny, sharp-tongued contemporary romance with a soft landing.
book.book470.title: Great Expectations
book.book470.author: Charles Dickens
book.book470.description: Pip feeds a convict out on the marshes, later comes into money from a source he is certain he understands, and learns what being a gentleman costs. Miss Havisham's stopped clocks are worth the trip alone.
book.book471.title: Heinemann Mathematics
book.book471.author: Scottish Primary Mathematics Group
book.book471.description: Thirty-odd pages of primary school sums: number lines, shape work and neat rows of exercises to be filled in with a pencil. One thin booklet from a long classroom series, and no fun was budgeted for.
book.book472.title: How Winston Delivered Christmas; A Christmas Story in Twenty-Four-and-a-Half Chapters
book.book472.author: Alex T. Smith
book.book472.description: One small mouse finds a letter addressed to Father Christmas and decides it simply must be delivered. Twenty-four and a half chapters, one per December day, with crafts and recipes tucked in between them.
book.book473.title: Howl, and Other Poems
book.book473.author: Allen Ginsberg
book.book473.description: Forty-four pages of Beat verse that went on trial for obscenity: long howling lines about madness, poverty, queer desire and the machine that eats the young. Poetry written to be read out loud.
book.book474.title: I Capture the Castle
book.book474.author: Dodie Smith
book.book474.description: Cassandra keeps a journal from a decaying castle her family cannot afford to heat, and two American landlords turn up to complicate everybody's affections. Funny, broke, and very good on being seventeen.
book.book475.title: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
book.book475.author: Maya Angelou
book.book475.description: Between a grandmother's store in Arkansas and a mother in St Louis, a girl stops speaking for years after an assault and reads her way back to a voice. Told plainly, which is exactly why it hurts.
book.book476.title: I, Robot
book.book476.author: Isaac Asimov
book.book476.description: Three laws are built into every positronic brain to keep robots safe, and every story here is a machine obeying them perfectly into some fresh disaster. Puzzle-box science fiction, told by a robopsychologist with no patience for sentiment.
book.book477.title: If Beale Street Could Talk
book.book477.author: James Baldwin
book.book477.description: Nineteen, pregnant, and trying to get the father of her child out of a cell he was put in on a lie. A love story squeezed inside a legal nightmare, under two hundred pages of Harlem voices and rage.
book.book478.title: If Tomorrow Comes
book.book478.author: Sidney Sheldon
book.book478.description: Framed, imprisoned and stripped of everything, Tracy Whitney leaves that cell with a talent for elaborate revenge and a taste for other people's jewels. Big, glossy, propulsive caper storytelling.
book.book479.title: Inkheart
book.book479.author: Cornelia Funke
book.book479.description: Meggie's father reads aloud so well that things come out of the book, and something goes in to take their place. Years later the villain he loosed comes looking. A love letter to reading with real menace in it.
book.book480.title: Jane Eyre
book.book480.author: Charlotte Brontë
book.book480.description: Plain, poor and not remotely meek, Jane takes a governess post at Thornfield and falls for an employer whose house keeps something awake at night. Gothic, bitter, and fierce about being treated as an equal.
book.book481.title: Jean Dubuffet
book.book481.author: Jean Dubuffet
book.book481.description: Seventy-odd pages of plates and commentary on a painter's work, the kind of slim catalogue an exhibition leaves behind. Plain in tone, niche by design, and a small treasure if the pictures are your pictures.
book.book482.title: Henry VI, Part 1
book.book482.author: William Shakespeare
book.book482.description: England loses France while its nobles bicker at home, and two roses plucked in a garden mark the factions that will tear the kingdom apart. First play of Shakespeare's trilogy about a boy king's reign.
book.book483.title: Henry VI, Part 3
book.book483.author: William Shakespeare
book.book483.description: Wars of the Roses at full boil: fathers kill sons, a queen leads armies, and a limping duke starts counting the bodies between himself and the crown. Third play of the trilogy, and by far the bloodiest.
book.book484.title: Richard II
book.book484.author: William Shakespeare
book.book484.description: Convinced God put the crown on his head, a young king banishes the wrong cousin and seizes the wrong inheritance. Shakespeare's history in verse throughout, more interested in the man than in the battles.
book.book485.title: Legendborn; The Legendborn Cycle #1
book.book485.author: Tracy Deonn
book.book485.description: Grieving her mother, Bree starts early college and finds a secret society of students descended from Arthur's knights. Arthurian legend collides with Black Southern rootwork, and the magic in her own blood answers first.
book.book486.title: Les Miserables
book.book486.author: Victor Hugo
book.book486.description: Stolen bread costs Valjean nineteen years, and a policeman who mistakes law for morality will not stop following him. Barricades, sewers and street children, plus long detours before the plot resumes.
book.book487.title: Letters from Egypt; 1862-1869
book.book487.author: Lucie Duff Gordon
book.book487.description: Sent to Egypt for her lungs, an Englishwoman settles at Luxor, learns Arabic and writes home about her neighbours, their taxes and their donkeys. Warm, gossipy letters from someone who never came back well.
book.book488.title: Letters of Bookstonbury
book.book488.author: Allatheena Jeon
book.book488.description: After her grandmother's death, a quiet librarian inherits a mobile bookshop. She plans to sell it - until she finds a hidden compartment beneath the floorboards, with old, unsent letters addressed to people all over town, uncovering stories of love, loss, and hope.
book.book489.title: The Library Book
book.book489.author: Susan Orlean
book.book489.description: Fire gutted the Los Angeles Central Library and the arson case never quite closed. Part investigation, part civic history, part ode to what libraries hold and to the people who would rather they burned.
book.book490.title: The Long Way to a Small Angry Planet; Wayfarers #1
book.book490.author: Becky Chambers
book.book490.description: Sign on with the Wayfarer, a battered tunnelling ship whose multispecies crew punch wormholes through space and bicker like family. The long haul to a war-torn planet matters less than who you share the galley with.
book.book491.title: Looking for Alaska
book.book491.author: John Green
book.book491.description: Miles leaves Florida for an Alabama boarding school hunting a Great Perhaps, and finds pranks, cheap wine and a girl named Alaska. Teenage wit for half the book, then a grief nobody is ready for.
book.book492.title: Lord of the Flies
book.book492.author: William Golding
book.book492.description: Schoolboys wash up on an island with a conch, a fire and no adults, and demonstrate how fast rules rot. Short, cold, and far nastier than the survival adventure the first chapter seems to promise.
book.book493.title: A Man for All Seasons
book.book493.author: Robert Bolt
book.book493.description: Thomas More will not swear the oath, and everyone from his king to his own daughter tries to talk him round. A play made almost entirely of argument, with a Common Man shifting scenery and picking sides.
book.book494.title: Maria Stuart
book.book494.author: Friedrich Schiller
book.book494.description: Two queens, one garden: Mary Stuart imprisoned and condemned, and the cousin who must decide whether to sign. Schiller's verse tragedy stages the meeting history never allowed them, and it burns.
book.book495.title: Matilda
book.book495.author: Roald Dahl
book.book495.description: Her parents treat reading as a disease and her headmistress throws children by the pigtails, but a small girl with a library card and a peculiar talent behind her eyes evens the score. Wickedly funny revenge.
book.book496.title: A Matter of Oaths
book.book496.author: Helen S. Wright
book.book496.description: Commander Rallya hires a web officer whose memory was legally erased for a crime he cannot remember, then learns two rival emperors want him back. Space opera with a slow-burn romance between men.
book.book497.title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
book.book497.author: Ransom Riggs
book.book497.description: After his grandfather dies raving about monsters, a teenager follows the old photographs to a ruined house on a Welsh island where the same day keeps repeating. Built around genuinely eerie found snapshots.
book.book498.title: Mont-Saint-Michel and Chartres
book.book498.author: Henry Adams
book.book498.description: Two great churches, read as the mind of an age: stone, glass and the cult of the Virgin taken as seriously as any philosophy. Dense, rapturous, closer to a long poem about medieval faith than to a guidebook.
book.book499.title: Mother Night
book.book499.author: Kurt Vonnegut
book.book499.description: Howard Campbell broadcast Nazi propaganda and passed coded messages to the Allies in the same sentence. Now he waits in an Israeli cell, writing it down. The coldest joke: you are what you pretend to be.
book.book500.title: The Mousetrap and Other Plays
book.book500.author: Agatha Christie
book.book500.description: Eight stage whodunnits in one brick of a book, headed by the snowed-in guesthouse thriller still running in London. Curtain-line reveals that generations of audiences have politely refused to spoil.
book.book501.title: Mrs. Dalloway
book.book501.author: Virginia Woolf
book.book501.description: One June day in London: Clarissa Dalloway shops for her party while a shell-shocked veteran across the city comes apart. Consciousness rendered hour by hour, with Big Ben striking over everybody.
book.book502.title: Much Ado About Nothing
book.book502.author: William Shakespeare
book.book502.description: Beatrice and Benedick would rather trade insults than admit anything, so their friends build a trap out of overheard gossip. Comedy in which slander nearly wrecks a wedding and wit repairs it.
book.book503.title: Night and Day
book.book503.author: Virginia Woolf
book.book503.description: Katharine keeps house for a famous poet's legacy and does mathematics in secret, engaged to one man and pulled toward another. Woolf at her most conventional: a long, clear-eyed courtship novel.
book.book504.title: Night Sky with Exit Wounds
book.book504.author: Ocean Vuong
book.book504.description: Poems moving between a father's war in Vietnam, a son's desire for other boys in small-town America, and the wreckage handed down between them. Lean, image-packed verse from a debut that earned its noise.
book.book505.title: On Beauty
book.book505.author: Zadie Smith
book.book505.description: Two feuding art historians, one liberal and one conservative, collide when their families tangle in a New England college town. Campus novel with marriage, race and class in the crossfire, and real jokes.
book.book506.title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
book.book506.author: Ocean Vuong
book.book506.description: Written as a letter to a mother who cannot read it: nail salon shifts in Hartford, a grandmother's war, a first love lost to opioids. A poet's prose, unsparing about violence and tenderness alike.
book.book507.title: Orlando
book.book507.author: Virginia Woolf
book.book507.description: An Elizabethan nobleman lives three centuries without ageing much, then wakes one morning as a woman and finds it mildly inconvenient. Mock biography, footnotes included, arguing that gender is costume.
book.book508.title: Othello
book.book508.author: William Shakespeare
book.book508.description: Passed over for promotion, Iago sets out to destroy his general using nothing but suggestion, a lost handkerchief and patience. Shakespeare's tightest tragedy, and the hardest one to sit through.
book.book509.title: P.S. I Still Love You
book.book509.author: Jenny Han
book.book509.description: Lara Jean's fake relationship turned real, and now a second old love letter answers back. Sweet, scrapbooking, endlessly overthinking, she has to work out which boy she actually wants. Series, book two.
book.book510.title: Pageboy
book.book510.author: Elliot Page
book.book510.description: Fame arriving before the self does: a memoir of growing up on film sets, staying closeted through an awards campaign, and the relief of finally saying who he is. Told in fragments rather than a tidy arc.
book.book511.title: Parable of the Sower
book.book511.author: Octavia E. Butler
book.book511.description: Lauren Olamina feels other people's pain in her own body, a bad gift in a California where the walls around her neighbourhood are failing. Out of the collapse she starts writing a religion called Earthseed.
book.book512.title: Persepolis; The Story of a Childhood
book.book512.author: Marjane Satrapi
book.book512.description: Growing up in Tehran as the revolution hardens, drawn in stark black and white by a girl who keeps asking the wrong questions. A graphic memoir, funny and then suddenly not, about childhood under a new regime.
book.book513.title: Peter Pan in Kensington Gardens
book.book513.author: J. M. Barrie
book.book513.description: Before the pirates and the crocodile, Peter was a week-old baby who flew out of the nursery window and settled in among the birds and fairies of a London park. Lyrical, wistful, stranger than the play it became.
book.book515.title: Prince Caspian; The Return to Narnia
book.book515.author: C.S. Lewis
book.book515.description: Centuries have passed in Narnia since the four children last left it, and the talking beasts have gone into hiding. A horn sounds, and the four are pulled back to help a young prince claim a stolen throne.
book.book516.title: The Princess Bride
book.book516.author: William Goldman
book.book516.description: Farm boy loves princess, pirates intervene, and a swordsman with a lifelong grudge counts the seconds. Presented as the good bits of a fat foreign classic, with the boring parts cheerfully cut out.
book.book517.title: Saga; Volume 9
