book.book517.author: Brian K. Vaughan & Fiona Staples
book.book517.description: Volume nine of the space opera comic where two soldiers from opposite sides raise a daughter on the run. Staples draws wonders and horrors with the same brush, and this one is short, tender and not remotely safe.
book.book518.title: Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little Life (#1)
book.book518.author: Bryan Lee O'Malley
book.book518.description: Toronto slacker, bad bassist, dating a high schooler, suddenly obsessed with a girl who rollerblades through his dreams. Then her first evil ex crashes the gig. Comics with video-game logic and real bruises.
book.book519.title: Sense and Sensibility
book.book519.author: Jane Austen
book.book519.description: Two sisters lose the family house and must marry well: one locks her feelings away, the other broadcasts hers and pays for it. Comedy about money that keeps pretending to be about love.
book.book520.title: Sister Outsider
book.book520.author: Audre Lorde
book.book520.description: Essays and speeches by a Black lesbian poet on anger, silence, erotic power and what difference is actually for. Arguments sharpened at the podium and still quoted at every protest. Non fiction that asks something of you.
book.book521.title: Starstruck; (Deluxe Edition)
book.book521.author: Elaine Lee & Michael Kaluta
book.book521.description: Kaluta's baroque line work and Lee's dense, footnoted satire make this space opera famously demanding. Collected at last in one slab, it rewards exactly the sort of reader who enjoys decoding a page.
book.book522.title: Stormbreaker
book.book522.author: Anthony Horowitz
book.book522.description: His uncle dies in a car crash that was nothing of the kind, and a fourteen-year-old discovers the holiday hobbies he was taught were spy training all along. Gadgets, a billionaire, a first mission. Book one.
book.book523.title: Sula
book.book523.author: Toni Morrison
book.book523.description: Nel stays in the Ohio hill town and marries; Sula leaves for ten years and returns scandalous. Their friendship survives nearly everything. Morrison on a Black neighbourhood and the cost of being free.
book.book524.title: The Sunlit Man
book.book524.author: Brandon Sanderson
book.book524.description: On a world where sunrise burns everything it touches, cities keep moving and a hunted drifter sells his labour just to stay ahead of the light. Sanderson at his bleakest, with the Cosmere humming underneath.
book.book525.title: Supernova; Renegades #3
book.book525.author: Marissa Meyer
book.book525.description: Closing book of a superhero trilogy in which the line between the costumed council that rules the city and the outlaws who oppose it keeps blurring. Long, twisty, and aimed squarely at a final showdown.
book.book526.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
book.book526.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
book.book526.description: Twelve short cases out of the Baker Street rooms: a scandalous photograph, a red-headed clerk, a band of speckled dread. The template every detective story since has been politely stealing from.
book.book527.title: The Book of Tea
book.book527.author: Okakura Kakuzo
book.book527.description: Why should a bowl of tea explain a whole civilisation? Because the tearoom holds its art, its manners and its quiet. A slim classic written to show the West what it had been too busy to notice.
book.book528.title: The Book of the City of Ladies
book.book528.author: Christine de Pizan
book.book528.description: Three crowned allegories visit a discouraged writer and set her to building a walled city out of the lives of women worth defending. Medieval argument, example after example, answering the slanders of its day.
book.book529.title: Book of Yokai ; Mysterious Creatures of Japanese Folklore
book.book529.author: Michael Dylan Foster & Shinonome Kijin
book.book529.description: Japanese folklore's monsters catalogued and explained: shape-shifting foxes, river imps, creatures born out of neglected household objects. A scholarly survey with a real feel for why these stories stuck.
book.book530.title: The Canterbury Tales
book.book530.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
book.book530.description: Pilgrims riding to Canterbury pass the time with a story contest: knightly romance, filth, sermons, and a fart joke that has outlived several empires. Verse, unfinished, and rowdier than school lets on.
book.book531.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
book.book531.author: Alexandre Dumas
book.book531.description: Framed on his wedding day, Edmond Dantes spends fourteen years in a sea fortress, walks out rich under a borrowed name, and takes his time. Twelve hundred pages of patient, delicious revenge.
book.book532.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
book.book532.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book.book532.description: Nine companions leave Rivendell carrying one small gold ring the wrong way, toward the only fire that can unmake it. The opening volume that set the shape of nearly every quest fantasy written since.
book.book533.title: The Girl Who Played with Fire
book.book533.author: Stieg Larsson
book.book533.description: Three bodies, a magazine investigation into trafficking about to go to print, and a hunted young hacker the whole of Sweden has decided is guilty. Second in the trilogy, and it runs harder than the first.
book.book534.title: The Green Ember; Book 1
book.book534.author: S.D. Smith & Zach Franzen
book.book534.description: Heather and Picket are rabbits whose ordinary afternoon ends with their home in ruins and their family scattered. Swords, secret havens and a kingdom worth rebuilding, told for younger readers with a straight face.
book.book535.title: The Green Mile
book.book535.author: Stephen King
book.book535.description: Cold Mountain's death row runs on routine until a huge, weeping prisoner arrives with hands that can undo harm. A tame mouse, a cruel guard, and a miracle nobody on the block can afford to believe in.
book.book536.title: Greenglass House; Book 1
book.book536.author: Kate Milford & Jaime Zollars
book.book536.description: Winter at a smugglers' inn should be quiet, but guests keep arriving, small things keep vanishing, and the innkeepers' son teams up with a stranger to work out which of the stories are true.
book.book537.title: The Gunslinger
book.book537.author: Stephen King
book.book537.description: Roland crosses a desert that never ends, chasing a man in black across a world that has moved on. Part western, part quest, and the opening move of King's very long march toward the Dark Tower.
book.book538.title: The House with a Clock in Its Walls
book.book538.author: John Bellairs
book.book538.description: The shabby uncle who takes in an orphaned boy turns out to be a wizard, and something ticks inside the plaster of his mansion, counting toward a very bad end. Creaky, gothic, and pitched at nervous readers.
book.book539.title: How Did Whales Get So Big?; An Other Curious Questions about Animals, Nature, Geology and Planet Earth
book.book539.author: MinuteEarth
book.book539.description: Why did whales end up so enormous? Bite-sized illustrated answers to the questions kids actually ask about animals, weather and rocks, from the crew behind the science cartoons. Silly drawings, careful science.
book.book540.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
book.book540.author: C. S. Lewis
book.book540.description: Four children, one wartime evacuation, and a wardrobe that opens onto a country locked in endless winter. Talking beasts, a lion who is not tame, and the first door anyone ever walked through into Narnia.
book.book541.title: Listen for the Lie
book.book541.author: Amy Tintera
book.book541.description: Everyone back home is certain Lucy killed her best friend. Lucy cannot remember that night at all, and now a true crime podcaster has arrived to dig the whole thing up. Wry, mean, very hard to put down.
book.book542.title: The Lost Continent
book.book542.author: C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne
book.book542.description: Atlantis in its last days, told by a soldier-priest: palace intrigue, monstrous beasts and a ruler who claims to be a goddess. Lost-world adventure of the old school, pulp grandeur and doom included.
book.book543.title: The Odyssey
book.book543.author: Homer, transl. by Knox & Fagles
book.book543.description: Ten years to get home from Troy, by way of a cyclops, a witch, a whirlpool, and a wife stalling a houseful of suitors. Verse built to be spoken aloud, in a translation quick enough to prove the point.
book.book544.title: Oh, Mary!
book.book544.author: Cole Escola
book.book544.description: Mary Todd Lincoln wants one thing in this gleefully filthy comedy: to be a cabaret star. Her husband would prefer she stayed upstairs. Short, fast and very queer, set in the last weeks of the war.
book.book545.title: Olivetti
book.book545.author: Allie Millington
book.book545.description: Olivetti is a typewriter who remembers every word typed on him, and he breaks his kind's only rule when the mother of the house disappears. Her son and a pawnshop girl follow the trail. Odd, funny, for kids.
book.book546.title: The Outsider
book.book546.author: Stephen King
book.book546.description: Everything says the beloved coach murdered a child, and everything says he was somewhere else entirely. Both sets of evidence hold up. Procedural at first, then quietly, horribly frightening.
book.book547.title: The Poetry of Architecture
book.book547.author: John Ruskin
book.book547.description: An early essay on cottages and villas, arguing that a building belongs to its landscape or it belongs nowhere. Dense prose, close attention to stone and hillside, and a young critic already certain of his eye.
book.book548.title: Pollyanna; Book 1
book.book548.author: Eleanor H. Porter
book.book548.description: An orphan lands on a stiff aunt who never wanted her and disarms a whole town with the glad game, finding something to be pleased about in everything. Sweet enough to ache, and the series starts here.
book.book549.title: The Return of the King
book.book549.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book.book549.description: Everything converges at once: the siege of a white city, a last hopeless march to the Black Gate, and two small figures still climbing in the dark. The final volume, and it earns its very long goodbye.
book.book550.title: The Scarecrow of Oz
book.book550.author: L. Frank Baum
book.book550.description: Swallowed by a whirlpool, a girl and her sailor friend wash up on the road to Jinxland, where a nasty king rules and a princess has had her heart frozen. The straw-stuffed hero arrives to sort it out.
book.book551.title: The Shadow of the Wind
book.book551.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
book.book551.description: In postwar Barcelona a boy adopts a forgotten novel and finds that someone has been burning every copy of its author's work. A labyrinth of bookshops, ruined mansions, old cruelties and first love.
book.book552.title: The Silent Patient
book.book552.author: Alex Michaelides
book.book552.description: Her husband is shot dead, and the painter who did it never speaks again. Years into her confinement a psychotherapist talks his way onto the ward, certain he can reach her. Clean, cold, engineered to blindside you.
book.book553.title: The Snowy Day
book.book553.author: Ezra Jack Keats
book.book553.description: Snow overnight, and a boy in a red snowsuit goes out to make tracks, knock the drifts off a tree and save a snowball in his pocket. Collage pictures, very few words, perfect for the smallest listeners.
book.book554.title: So Easy So Good
book.book554.author: Kylie Sakaida
book.book554.description: Weeknight cooking for people who are tired: short ingredient lists, balanced plates, and recipes that do not need a second pan. Cheerful, practical, and aimed at whoever is standing in the kitchen at seven.
book.book555.title: Stone Butch Blues
book.book555.author: Leslie Feinberg
book.book555.description: Jess Goldberg grows up butch in 1950s Buffalo, finds family in the bars and pays for it in police raids and factory jobs. A novel about passing, hormones and survival, written from inside that life.
book.book556.title: The Stones of Venice
book.book556.author: John Ruskin
book.book556.description: Every capital and arch in Venice put on trial, with Gothic craftsmanship acquitted and the Renaissance found guilty of killing the joy of the workman. Learned, opinionated, unhurried; one volume of a larger survey.
book.book557.title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
book.book557.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
book.book557.description: Respectable London hides plenty, and a lawyer pulling at a friend's strange will finds a brutish young man who stands to benefit from it. Slim, feverish horror about what the decent self keeps in the cellar.
book.book558.title: The Two Towers
book.book558.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book.book558.description: Split paths: one half rides with the horse-lords into a wizard's war, the other creeps east behind a guide nobody sensible would trust. The middle volume, where the losses start landing for real.
book.book559.title: The Westing Game
book.book559.author: Ellen Raskin
book.book559.description: Sixteen tenants of a new apartment tower are named heirs to a millionaire's fortune, paired off at random and handed clues that make no sense alone. A puzzle that plays completely fair. Bring paper!
book.book560.title: Towards a New Architecture
book.book560.author: Le Corbusier
book.book560.description: A manifesto that holds up ocean liners, aeroplanes and grain silos as models for how houses should be built, and calls the home a machine for living in. Polemical, repetitive, and impossible to ignore since.
book.book561.title: Ugly Love
book.book561.author: Colleen Hoover
book.book561.description: Tate agrees to two rules with the pilot across the hall: no questions about his past, no expectations about a future. Alternating chapters reveal why he set them. Romance built to hurt before it heals.
book.book562.title: Understanding Comics; The Invisible Art
book.book562.author: Scott McCloud
book.book562.description: Comics explained in comics form, a cartoon narrator walking you through panels, gutters and the way your brain fills the gaps between them. The theory book that made a whole medium take itself seriously.
book.book563.title: The Unexpected Mrs. Pollifax; Mrs. Pollifax #1
book.book563.author: Dorothy Gilman
book.book563.description: A New Jersey widow bored with her garden club volunteers as a spy, and to everyone's alarm the agency says yes. The simple errand abroad goes wrong at once: charming, dated and thoroughly game.
book.book564.title: White Night
book.book564.author: Jim Butcher
book.book564.description: Chicago's lesser practitioners are turning up dead in ways that look like suicide, and the only wizard in the phone book takes the case. Another Dresden outing: wisecracks, vampire politics, and real collateral damage.
book.book565.title: Witch Wood
book.book565.author: John Buchan
book.book565.description: Sent to a moorland parish in Covenanting Scotland, a young minister finds his own flock slipping into the woods at night for older rites. Bleak, beautiful, and hard on anyone expecting goodness to win.
book.book566.title: Z for Zachariah
book.book566.author: Robert C. O'Brian
book.book566.description: After the war a teenage girl farms the sheltered valley she believes is the last living place on earth, until smoke shows on the ridge and a stranger in a safe suit walks in. A diary that tightens page by page.
book.book567.title: Zaha Hadid
book.book567.author: Zaha Hadid
book.book567.description: One architect's portfolio in print: elevations, sketches and plates, laid out with barely a word of commentary to get in the way. Slim, niche, and likely to end up permanently open on a studio desk.
book.book568.title: Adventures of A Wild Child
book.book568.author: Gina Grayson Hunt
book.book568.description: Join the escapades of a free-spirited wanderer as they navigate love, self-discovery, and countless adventures in this captivating memoir.
book.book569.title: An Explorer's Guide to Georgetown
book.book569.author: Zheng Greene
book.book569.description: Discover the secrets of Georgetown in this fun and beautifully illustrated guide. Explore its history, indulge in local cuisine, and soak up the vibrant lifestyle.
book.book570.title: An Unkindness of Ghosts
book.book570.author: Rivers Solomon
book.book570.description: Aster lives in the lower decks of a generation ship run like a plantation, healing people the overseers would rather see punished. Her dead mother's notebooks hint at where the ship is really going.
book.book571.title: Catching Carps
book.book571.author: Nigel Carpum
book.book571.description: Reel in this absolute catch of a book, because Carpum's fishing trip is something special! Weaving together carp facts, personal philosophy, and globetrotting tales, the author shares all his wisdom.
book.book572.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 1
book.book572.author: Ash Axbridge
book.book572.description: Discover a treasure trove of knowledge in this captivating encyclopaedia! From A as in Academia to C as in Crime, learn more about what makes the world of books go round.
book.book573.title: Gemology: A Study in Ruby
book.book573.author: Ellie Obsidia
book.book573.description: Unearth the secrets of the dazzling gemstones in this sparkling study of gemology. A challenging academic text from an expert of the field.
book.book574.title: The Ghost Map; A Street, a City, An Epidemic and the Hidden Power of Urban Networks
book.book574.author: Steven Johnson
book.book574.description: London, cholera, and a doctor with a map: how one Soho outbreak was traced to a single water pump and overturned the idea that disease drifts in on bad air. Popular science that doubles as a case for cities.
book.book575.title: Hiking Trails in Bookston Bay
book.book575.author: Val Bomier
book.book575.description: Get lost and find yourself amidst the stunning natural beauty of Bookston Bay's secret hiking trails. Stunning coastal vistas await around every corner!
book.book576.title: Into the Sunset: The Magical West
book.book576.author: Cemal M. Fahmy
book.book576.description: Explore the mythical and exotic lands of Western Europe. This satirical travelogue lets you in on the secret wisdom and mysterious culture of the West.
book.book577.title: My Travels In East Africa
book.book577.author: Tao Ryota
book.book577.description: From Burundi to Uganda, an ageing adventurer shares his eye-opening journey through Eastern Africa, learning life's greatest lessons along the way.
book.book578.title: The Secret History of Bookstonbury
book.book578.author: H. A. Pennington
book.book578.description: An insight into the forgotten anecdotes of history, which was hugely popular in 1953 and still makes for an entertaining read. However, most of these historical "theories" have since been disproven.
book.book579.title: The Secret Island; The Secret Series #1
book.book579.author: Enid Blyton
book.book579.description: Four children, badly treated at home, row out to an island in a lake and set up house with a cow, a rowboat and a willow shelter. Cosy runaway adventure, all raspberries and secrets, and book one.
book.book580.title: Selected Stories of Anton Chekhov
book.book580.author: A. Chekhov, L. Volokhonsky & R. Pevear
book.book580.description: Story after story catches people mid-compromise: a seaside affair, a bored doctor, a dog, a funeral, and nothing tied off. Endings that simply stop rather than conclude, and they follow you around for days.
book.book581.title: Hélène
book.book581.author: St. Bookston
book.book581.description: A romantic reinterpretation of the Illiad. Hélène, a 16th-century version of Helen of Troy, has the chance to forever change the trajectory of her life and love. A historical play and a St. Bookston classic for a reason!
book.book582.title: Hello Lighthouse
book.book582.author: Sophie Blackall
book.book582.description: Inside a round tower on a rock, a keeper trims the wick, fills the log and waits out fog and ice while his family grows. Watercolours built for the shape of the page, and a quiet look at work being made obsolete.
book.book583.title: A Collection of Poems
book.book583.author: St. Bookston
book.book583.description: A collection of Saint Bookston's greatest works of poetry, including Ashen Grey , Prometheus' Regrets , and Last Breaths .
book.book584.title: A Senseless Power
book.book584.author: St. Bookston
book.book584.description: A timeless family drama by the brilliant Bookston. The three sons of a rich merchant family are vying for their powerful mother's approval. Will their quest for the matriarch's position be worth the destruction they sow on their ways to the top?
book.book585.title: On the Naturale Flora of Bookstonborough
book.book585.author: St. Bookston
book.book585.description: A taxonomy of the flora of Bookston Bay from the late 16th century. With hand-drawn illustrations by the polymath Saint Bookston.
book.book586.title: Rebecca
book.book586.author: Daphne du Maurier
book.book586.description: A new bride reaches Manderley to find the first wife's monogram on everything and a housekeeper who worships her memory. Dread assembled out of furniture and menus, and nobody lets her forget she is second.
book.book587.title: Carmilla
book.book587.author: J. Sheridan Le Fanu
book.book587.description: Lonely in a Styrian castle, Laura finally gets the companion she longed for, and promptly begins to sicken. This vampire novella came a quarter century before Dracula and stays the more intimate book.
book.book588.title: Anne of Green Gables
book.book588.author: L.M. Montgomery
book.book588.description: Matthew and Marilla asked for a farm boy and got a red-headed talker who renames the landscape and apologises at enormous length. Warm, funny, and the opening of a very long series.
book.book589.title: Guards! Guards!
book.book589.author: Terry Pratchett
book.book589.description: Someone has summoned a dragon to Ankh-Morpork to install a puppet king, and the city's drunk, undermanned Night Watch is all that stands in the way. Where Discworld grew a conscience and stayed funny.
book.book590.title: The Haunting of Hill House
book.book590.author: Shirley Jackson
book.book590.description: Hill House takes in four people for a study of the supernatural and reserves its attention for the loneliest of them. Cold hands, chalked walls, and dread that works by never quite showing itself.
book.book591.title: Dinosaurs and other Prehistoric Life
book.book591.author: Anusuya Chinsamy-Turan
book.book591.description: Big illustrated spreads walking back through deep time, era by era, with skeletons, reconstructions and all the creatures that were not dinosaurs but get lumped in anyway. Shelf reference for an obsessed kid.
book.book592.title: Newtonian Physics for Babies
book.book592.author: Chris Ferrie
book.book592.description: A board book explaining forces to an audience still working on sitting up: bold shapes, one idea per page, and a completely straight face. The joke is for the grown-up reading aloud, and it lands.
book.book593.title: The Adventures of Pippi Longstocking
book.book593.author: Astrid Lindgren
book.book593.description: Nine years old, strong enough to lift a horse, living alone with a monkey and a bag of gold while the grown-ups fuss. Episodic nonsense that adults read as chaos and children read as a manifesto.
book.book594.title: Codename Villanelle
book.book594.author: Luke Jennings
book.book594.description: An assassin with expensive taste and no conscience, and the intelligence officer who starts noticing a pattern nobody above her will admit exists. Lean, cold chase fiction, opening a short series.
book.book595.title: Coffee First, Then the World
book.book595.author: Jenny Graham
book.book595.description: Around the world by bicycle, alone and unsupported, chasing a record with a coffee stop wherever one could be found. A cheerful, self-deprecating adventure memoir that ends the way you want it to.
book.book596.title: Moominland Midwinter
book.book596.author: Tove Jansson
book.book596.description: Moomintroll wakes months early, alone in a hibernating house, and finds a whole winter world his family sleeps straight through. Strange company, cold light, and the gentlest lesson in being on your own.
book.book597.title: The Witch Boy
book.book597.author: Molly Knox Ostertag
book.book597.description: In Aster's family, girls learn witchery and boys learn to shapeshift, and nobody thinks to ask which he would rather do. A warm graphic novel about wanting the magic you were never assigned.
book.book598.title: The Bookshop Book
book.book598.author: Lucy Mangan
book.book598.description: Shop by shop, a warm tour of the places that sell books: the odd ones, the tiny ones, the ones that should not still be open. Light, browsable, and dangerous to anyone who already owns too many books.
book.book599.title: Borne
book.book599.author: Jeff VanderMeer
book.book599.description: Rachel scavenges a poisoned city ruled by a giant flying bear, and brings home a thing she names Borne. It grows. It learns to talk. Whether it is a person or a weapon may not end up being her call.
book.book600.title: Bookworm; A Memoir of Childhood Reading
book.book600.author: Jen Campbell
book.book600.description: Growing up is retold here through the books that did the raising, one shelf at a time. Funny, fond and easy company, the kind of memoir that keeps nudging you towards a reread.
book.book601.title: What We Don't Talk About; When We Talk About Fat
book.book601.author: Aubrey Gordon
book.book601.description: Anti-fat bias treated as a structural problem rather than a personal failing: doctors, airline seats, hiring, and the language of concern. Part memoir, part argument, with the research stacked up behind it.
book.book602.title: Witch Hat Atelier; Volume 1
book.book602.author: Kamome Shirahama
book.book602.description: Coco learns that magic is not born into anyone: it is drawn, with ink and a steady hand. Taken on as an apprentice, she starts at the very bottom, in a manga whose artwork alone earns the shelf space.
book.book603.title: The Surgeon
book.book603.author: Tess Gerritsen
book.book603.description: Boston has a killer copying a dead man's methods, and the surgeon who survived the original is the one person who understands what is coming. Clinical, bloody, and the start of a long partnership.
book.book604.title: The Taking of Annie Thorne
book.book604.author: C.J Tudor
book.book604.description: Returning to the pit village he swore never to see again, a teacher takes the only job going, in the place where his sister vanished as a child and came home not quite herself. Bleak and brilliantly creepy.
book.book605.title: Tasting History; Explore the Past through 4,000 Years of Recipes
book.book605.author: Max Miller
book.book605.description: Historical recipes tested until they actually work, each with the history of the dish attached: ancient stews, medieval pies, wartime improvisation. A cookbook to read for pleasure and still cook from tonight.
book.book606.title: Happily Ever After Cookbook; Original Recipes for Book Lovers
book.book606.author: Various Authors
book.book606.description: Recipes built for readers, to be cooked with one hand and a novel propped open under the other. Slim, cheerful and deeply niche: exactly the gift for the friend whose kitchen doubles as a library.
book.book607.title: Cook As You Are; Recipes for Real Life, Hungry Cooks and Messy Kitchens
book.book607.author: Ruby Tandoh
book.book607.description: Cooking for the tired, the broke and the easily overwhelmed, with no lecture about doing it properly. Generous, unfussy recipes and a flat refusal to make anyone feel bad about a messy kitchen.
book.book608.title: Cook Korean!; A Comic Book with Recipes
book.book608.author: Robin Ha
book.book608.description: Kimchi, bibimbap and banchan taught in comic panels, every step drawn rather than described. Bright, funny and unexpectedly practical, whether or not you have cooked Korean food before.
book.book609.title: A Cook's Tour; Global Adventures in Extreme Cuisines
book.book609.author: Anthony Bourdain
book.book609.description: Chasing the perfect meal from Portugal to Vietnam, eating whatever the locals eat and arguing with anyone who calls it extreme. Restless, profane, and better on why people cook than most cookbooks manage.
book.book610.title: The Stonewall Reader
book.book610.author: The New York Public Library
book.book610.description: First-hand accounts from before, during and after the Stonewall uprising, pulled out of the archives: diaries, interviews, movement periodicals. An anthology that lets the people who were there do the talking.
book.book611.title: We Are Bridges; A Memoir
book.book611.author: Cassandra Lane
book.book611.description: Pregnancy sends a writer back through family silence toward a great-grandfather lost to a lynching, reconstructing what the records refuse to hold. A memoir moving between generations, close to poetry.
book.book612.title: We Solve Murders; Book 1
book.book612.author: Richard Osman
book.book612.description: Retired and happiest in his armchair, a private investigator is hauled off by his globe-trotting bodyguard daughter-in-law, and the bodies and the money follow. Warm, quick and extremely quotable.
book.book613.title: Hawaii's Story by Hawaii's Queen
book.book613.author: Lili'uokalani
book.book613.description: The last queen of Hawaii tells how her kingdom was taken: court life, the overthrow, her imprisonment, and an appeal addressed straight to American readers. Dignified, pointed, a primary source with a voice.
book.book614.title: Heartless
book.book614.author: Marissa Meyer
book.book614.description: Before the Queen of Hearts started shouting about heads, she was a girl who wanted to open a bakery and fell for the wrong court joker. Wonderland nonsense, sweet baking, and an ending that has to hurt.
book.book615.title: Botany in a Day; The Patterns Method of Plant Identification
book.book615.author: Thomas J. Elpel
book.book615.description: Learn the plant families instead of memorizing species and the whole meadow starts making sense. A workmanlike field guide to the patterns method, with keys, line drawings and notes on edible and medicinal use.
book.book616.title: The Boundless Sea; A Human History of the Oceans
book.book616.author: David Abulafia
book.book616.description: Human history retold from the water: outrigger canoes, monsoon traders, Dutch fleets, all the way to container ships. Over a thousand dense pages, and the detail piles up faster than the argument does.
book.book617.title: Boy's Life
book.book617.author: Robert R. McCammon
book.book617.description: One Alabama spring a milk round ends with a car sinking into a bottomless lake and a murdered man strapped inside. A long, magic-soaked memory of boyhood where wonder and horror share a street.
book.book618.title: The Boy, The Mole, The Fox and The Horse; (Book 1)
book.book618.author: Charlie Mackesy
book.book618.description: Four unlikely friends wander a bare landscape and talk about kindness, fear and cake. Handwritten lines under ink and watercolour drawings, meant to be opened anywhere rather than read straight through.
book.book619.title: Boys run the riot, Vol. 1
book.book619.author: Keito Gaku
book.book619.description: Ryo is a trans high schooler who only feels like himself in the clothes he chooses, until a loud new classmate proposes they launch a streetwear label together. Manga about fashion, pronouns and nerve.
book.book620.title: Boys run the riot, Vol. 1
book.book620.author: Keito Gaku
book.book620.description: Clothes are the one place Ryo gets read correctly. Building a streetwear brand from nothing with a classmate who asks no awkward questions opens this manga series about being trans and being sixteen.
book.book621.title: Breakfast at Tiffany's
book.book621.author: Truman Capote
book.book621.description: Holly Golightly arrives in an Upper East Side brownstone with a nameless cat, no fixed past and a talent for other people's money. Slim postwar novella, funnier and considerably sadder than the film.
book.book622.title: The Bright Sword
book.book622.author: Lev Grossman
book.book622.description: Collum reaches Camelot a fortnight too late: Arthur is dead and only the second-string knights are left. Long, learned and dryly funny about carrying on after the legend has already ended.
book.book623.title: British Boutique Hotels
book.book623.author: Gina Jackson
book.book623.description: Photographs and short write-ups of small British hotels worth booking, sorted so you can choose by mood and region. A coffee-table travel guide that works perfectly well as a pure daydreaming device.
book.book624.title: Brown Girl Dreaming
book.book624.author: Jacqueline Woodson
book.book624.description: A childhood told in short poems, split between a South Carolina grandmother's porch and a Brooklyn street, the civil rights era humming behind it. A memoir in verse that earns every single line break.
book.book625.title: The Bullet That Missed; A Thursday Murder Club Mystery #3
book.book625.author: Richard Osman
book.book625.description: Four pensioners from a retirement village cannot let go of a cold case out of local television, a body never found and a fortune unaccounted for. Third outing for the club, and one of them is being blackmailed.
book.book626.title: Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil
book.book626.author: V.E. Schwab
book.book626.description: Three women, centuries apart, turned into something that neither dies nor forgives. A sapphic vampire novel that is hungry in every sense, long, lush and thoroughly uninterested in redeeming anyone.
book.book627.title: A Buzz in the Meadows; The Natural History of a French Farm
book.book627.author: Dave Goulson
book.book627.description: Goulson buys a derelict farm in rural France and spends years counting what lives there: bees, deathwatch beetles, dragonflies. Field notes turned into companionable science, with a warning folded inside.
book.book628.title: Entangled Life; How Fungi Make Our Worlds, Change Our Minds & Shape Our Futures
book.book628.author: Merlin Sheldrake
book.book628.description: Fungi as the quiet infrastructure of life: networks trading with tree roots, lichens that are two organisms at once, truffle hunts and mind-altering mushrooms. Popular science with genuine wonder in it.
book.book629.title: Escape from Mr. Lemoncello's Library; Mr. Lemoncello's Library #1
book.book629.author: Chris Grabenstein
book.book629.description: Twelve lucky kids win a lock-in at the most extravagant library ever built, then learn the only way out is hidden somewhere in the shelves. Puzzles, games and book jokes at sprinting speed.
book.book630.title: The Origin of Species
book.book630.author: Charles Darwin
book.book630.description: Pigeons, barnacles and one long patient argument that species change by natural selection. Dense Victorian science, written before anyone knew what a gene was, and still the book everything after it answers to.
book.book631.title: Provence to Pondicherry; Recipes from France and Faraway
book.book631.author: Tessa Kiros
book.book631.description: French cooking followed wherever French ships went: Provence, Vietnam, Pondicherry, the islands, with photographs as slow and warm as the recipes. A travel cookbook to read in bed and cook from on Sunday.
book.book632.title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
book.book632.author: Becky Chambers
book.book632.description: Dex serves tea and sympathy from a wagon until a robot walks out of the wilderness with one question: what do people need? Short, kind, and quietly radical about rest, in a future that chose gentleness.
book.book633.title: Pygmalion
book.book633.author: George Bernard Shaw
book.book633.description: A phonetics professor bets he can pass a flower girl off as a duchess by correcting her vowels, and never once asks what she is meant to do afterwards. Brisk, talky, merciless about the English class system.
book.book634.title: A Raisin in the Sun
book.book634.author: Lorraine Hansberry
book.book634.description: Ten thousand dollars of insurance money lands in a cramped South Side apartment, and every Younger wants it spent differently. The first play by a Black woman staged on Broadway, and still the sharpest.
book.book635.title: The Royal Horticultural Society Encyclopedia of Gardening
book.book635.author: Royal Horticultural Society
book.book635.description: Soil preparation, pruning, propagation, pests: hundreds of pages of authoritative reference, illustrated step by step, arranged so you can look up one problem and fix it this weekend. Charm was not the goal.
book.book636.title: The Ruins of Gorlan; (Ranger's Apprentice #1)
book.book636.author: John Flanagan
book.book636.description: Will is too small for battleschool, so he is apprenticed to the kingdom's grim, sarcastic Ranger instead: a bow, a grey cloak and a great deal of unglamorous practice. First of a very readable series.
book.book637.title: Russians in Alaska, 1732-1867
book.book637.author: Lydia T. Black
book.book637.description: Russian America reconstructed from the archives: fur company politics, Orthodox missions, and the Native communities whose part the older accounts left out. Academic history, footnoted, worth the effort.
book.book638.title: Annihilation
book.book638.author: Jeff VanderMeer
book.book638.description: Four women walk into Area X, a stretch of coast that has swallowed every expedition sent before them. The biologist keeps notes. What waits in a tunnel going down is best met without preparation.
book.book639.title: Anna Karenina
book.book639.author: Leo Tolstoy
book.book639.description: Anna leaves a cold marriage for a cavalry officer and watches Petersburg society shut its doors, while a landowner named Levin digs for meaning in his fields. Eight hundred pages, none of them idle.
book.book640.title: The Fisherman
book.book640.author: John Langan
book.book640.description: Two widowers take up fishing to get through their grief, and a stranger's story about a certain creek should have stopped them going. Slow, literary cosmic horror that earns every inch of its dread.
book.book641.title: The Sea Around Us
book.book641.author: Rachel Carson
book.book641.description: Oceans described with a naturalist's precision and a poet's ear: tides, currents, the dark of the deep, islands being born. Popular science from before the sonar maps, and the prose has not aged a day.
book.book642.title: The Sea Inside
book.book642.author: Philip Hoare
book.book642.description: Walking out from an English shore and somehow ending up among whales, ravens and drowned histories on the far side of the world. Nature writing that wanders where it likes, melancholy, funny, full of animals.
book.book643.title: Spirals in Time; The Secret Life and Curious Afterlife of Seashells
book.book643.author: Helen Scales
book.book643.description: Seashells as architecture, currency, dye and dinner: how molluscs build those spirals, and why humans have collected, traded and worn them for millennia. A marine biologist's tour, curious and companionable.
book.book644.title: Spring Clean
book.book644.author: Sabreen Islam
book.book644.description: Ninety-odd pages of contemporary poetry, finished in one sitting and better on the second pass. A quiet, niche collection for readers who want verse that sounds like now rather than like the syllabus.
book.book645.title: The Search; Avatar The Last Airbender (#4-6)
book.book645.author: Konietzko, DiMartino & Yang
book.book645.description: Zuko finally goes looking for his missing mother and takes his dangerously unstable sister along for the ride. Three Avatar comics in one volume, bright and funny until the family history bites.
book.book646.title: Wake; The Hidden History of Women-Led Slave Revolts
book.book646.author: Rebecca Hall & Hugo Martínez
book.book646.description: A historian hunts through court records and ship logs for the women who led revolts aboard slave ships, drawn as a graphic narrative that includes the search itself. Angry, rigorous, and hard to put down.
book.book647.title: The Magic Fish
book.book647.author: Trung Le Nguyen
book.book647.description: Tien cannot find the Vietnamese words to tell his mother he is gay, so mother and son keep reading fairy tales instead. Three versions of one tale braided through a graphic novel drawn in three colours.
book.book648.title: An Age of License; A Travelogue (#1)
book.book648.author: Lucy Knisley
book.book648.description: Drawn on the road: a young cartoonist takes a European book tour and turns the trains, cheese, flirtations and low-grade panic about the future into panels. Light, honest, and first of her travel comics.
book.book649.title: An Atlas of Countries that Don't Exist
book.book649.author: Nick Middleton
book.book649.description: Fifty places with flags, borders and governments that most of the world declines to recognize, each given a map and a few sober pages of history. Browsable geopolitics for anyone who likes an awkward border.
book.book650.title: An Experiment with an Air Pump
book.book650.author: Shelagh Stephenson
book.book650.description: One house in Newcastle, two centuries apart: Enlightenment gentlemen staging experiments for an audience, and a geneticist weighing what her research is for. Bones under the kitchen floor join them.
book.book651.title: This Was Our Pact
book.book651.author: Ryan Andrews
book.book651.description: On the autumn equinox the lanterns go down the river, and a pack of boys swears to follow them to the end. Most turn back. What waits for the two who keep going is stranger and kinder than expected.
book.book652.title: Thornhill
book.book652.author: Pam Smy
book.book652.description: Two girls, two eras, one shuttered children's home. A diary tells one half and wordless drawings tell the other, closing in on what happened behind those gates. Illustrated, spare and genuinely eerie.
book.book653.title: Three Bags Full; Sheep Detective Story #1
book.book653.author: Leonie Swann & Anthea Bell
book.book653.description: George the shepherd is found dead in his own meadow, so his flock sets out to investigate, led by the cleverest sheep in Ireland. Sheep logic applied to human wickedness, and far funnier than it sounds.
book.book654.title: Thumbelina
book.book654.author: Hans Christian Andersen
book.book654.description: Born in a tulip and no taller than a thumb, a girl is stolen by a toad, adopted by a mouse and promised to a mole before the swallows get a say. Short, strange, and kind to her in the end.
book.book655.title: Troglobites Don't Bite
book.book655.author: Mayara Ferreira
book.book655.description: What does life look like in total darkness? It's much more busy than you would think! Get to know the most fascinating cave-dwellers: from worms to snails, spiders, crustaceans, insects, fish, amphibians, and even the occasional mammalian visitor!
book.book656.title: How Many Castles in 7 Days?
book.book656.author: Stephen Jezek
book.book656.description: Stephen is a fan of castles, and he always manages to visit one wherever he travels. On his effective quest to see the most castles in only one week, Stephen compares the Czech Republic, Thuringia, and Wales in this hilarious travelogue.
book.book657.title: How to Stop Time
book.book657.author: Matt Haig
book.book657.description: Tom Hazard looks forty and has been alive for centuries, teaching history he personally watched happen. The society protecting people like him has one rule: never fall in love. Melancholy, and on the side of living.
book.book658.title: Dragon Ball; Volume 1
book.book658.author: Akira Toriyama
book.book658.description: Seven magic orbs scattered across the world will summon a dragon who grants a wish. A girl hunting them falls in with a boy who has a monkey tail and startling strength. Slapstick, tournaments, a long run ahead.
book.book659.title: Dragonology; The Complete Book of Dragons
book.book659.author: Ernest Drake
book.book659.description: Presented as the field notes of a nineteenth-century dragonologist, with flaps to lift, samples to handle and species charts to study. A short, gorgeous object for any child who wants dragons filed properly.
book.book660.title: Jujutsu Kaisen; Volume 1
book.book660.author: Gege Akutami
book.book660.description: Yuji Itadori swallows a rotting finger to save his friends and ends up sharing his body with a thousand-year-old curse. Sorcery school, grisly monsters, and a hero who insists everyone deserves a decent death.
book.book661.title: Ranma 1/2; Volume 1
book.book661.author: Rumiko Takahashi
book.book661.description: Cold water turns Ranma into a girl, hot water turns him back, and his father into a panda. Add an arranged engagement to a girl who despises boys, and the martial arts farce is up and running.
book.book662.title: Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint; Volume 1
book.book662.author: singNsong & UMI
book.book662.description: Kim Dokja is the only person who ever finished a very long, very bad web novel. When its apocalypse starts happening for real, being the one reader who knows the plot turns into the best weapon going.
book.book663.title: On the Banks of Plum Creek; (Little House, Book 4)
book.book663.author: Laura Ingalls Wilder
book.book663.description: A family moves into a dugout in the creek bank and stakes everything on a wheat crop that grasshoppers arrive to eat. Fourth in the series, and the weather is the real antagonist throughout.
book.book664.title: Sailor Moon; Volume 1
book.book664.author: Naoko Takeuchi
book.book664.description: Usagi is fourteen, bad at school and worse at waking up, until a talking cat hands her a brooch and a job saving the world. The volume that launched a thousand magical girls, and still charming.
book.book665.title: Ouran High School Host Club; Volume 1
book.book665.author: Bisco Hatori
book.book665.description: Haruhi, a scholarship student at a school for the absurdly rich, smashes a priceless vase and gets press-ganged into the campus host club to work off the debt. Shojo manga that cheerfully spoofs itself.
book.book666.title: My Lesbian Experience With Loneliness
book.book666.author: Nagata Kabi
book.book666.description: An autobiographical manga about depression, an eating disorder, and finally booking a female escort because nothing else had worked. Painfully candid, oddly funny, and drawn in relentlessly cheerful pink.
book.book667.title: Monster; Volume 1
book.book667.author: Naoki Urasawa
book.book667.description: Two patients, one surgeon, a single choice, and a lifetime spent paying for it. Cold adult suspense in comic form, set in Germany, opening a series that turns very, very dark.
book.book668.title: The Rose of Versailles
book.book668.author: Riyoko Ikeda
book.book668.description: Oscar was raised as a son to command the Royal Guard, and now protects a young queen at Versailles while France starves outside the gates. Landmark shojo manga: ballgowns, duels, revolution coming.
book.book669.title: FAKE; Volume 1
book.book669.author: Sanami Matoh
book.book669.description: Two New York detectives get partnered up: one all appetite and bad jokes, the other too polite to say no clearly. Cases cracked between flirtations in an early boys love manga with a crime-comedy pulse.
book.book670.title: Dickens at Christmas
book.book670.author: Charles Dickens
book.book670.description: Five Christmas stories with the ghosts left in: a miser walked through his own life by spirits, goblins in a bell tower, a chemist who wishes his memories away. Sentiment and haunting in equal measure.
